Instagram and Facebook are set to change forever if Meta loses a major child privacy trial going to court today.

The Meta Platforms case is set to begin with opening statements on Tuesday in a California federal court.

Attorneys general from California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey are pursuing significant financial damages alongside operational changes to Facebook and Instagram. Twenty-nine states launched legal action against the tech giant in 2023 over child safety and privacy, with 25 remaining states going to trial later. The business is also subject to state court claims.

The lawsuit accuses the social media company of contributing to a youth mental health crisis by deliberately designing features that leave children addicted to its platforms. It further argues that Meta routinely gathers data on children under 13 without the consent of their parents, in breach of federal law.

“This week, we’re in court with the largest consumer protection lawsuit in American history. We’ll show a jury that Meta concealed what it knew about the harm its products cause young people because looking away was more profitable,” said Kentucky Attorney General Russell Coleman in a statement.

Meta said it believes it has a strong case.

open image in gallery Colorado's Chief Trial Counsel Jason Slouthouber arrives at a Federal Courthouse Wednesday, Aug. 12, 2026, in Oakland, Calif. (AP Photo/Jeff Chiu) ( Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved )

“We are proud of our record in protecting teens on our platforms and the amount of effort that we’ve put into developing protections over the years, even before these cases were ever filed, and continuing to the present day. We look forward to showing the judge and the jury those facts in court,” the company said in a statement.

U.S. District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers in Oakland will oversee the proceedings, which are expected to last six to eight weeks, with Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and other executives and former employees testifying. Gonzalez Rogers, appointed to the bench by President Barack Obama in 2011, has overseen a bevy of complex, high-profile cases involving Big Tech. These include Elon Musk's lawsuit against OpenAI and its founders as well as Epic Games' lawsuit against Apple over its app store.

open image in gallery Colorado's Chief Trial Counsel Jason Slothouber and Division Chief of Kentucky's Consumer and Senior Protection Chris Lewis stand in line outside a federal courthouse where a trial over allegations that Meta designed Facebook and Instagram to be addictive to children takes place, in Oakland, California, U.S., August 12, 2026. REUTERS/Manuel Orbegozo ( Reuters )

The trial is the latest in an avalanche of lawsuits against Meta Platforms and other social media companies including Google’s YouTube, TikTok and Snap, over arguments that their platforms harm young people, illegally collect their data and are deliberately designed to addict them.

From Australia to Europe, countries move to curb children's social media access

Australia in December became the world's first country to ban social media for children under 16, blocking them from platforms including TikTok, Alphabet's YouTube ​and Meta's Instagram and Facebook.

Below is a summary of what countries and companies are doing to regulate access to social media amid mounting concerns over the impact of social media on children's health and safety.

AUSTRALIA

A landmark law forced major social media platforms to block minors under 16 from December 10, 2025, one of the world's toughest regulations targeting major tech platforms.

Companies that fail to comply could face penalties of up to A$49.5 million ($34.9 million).

BRITAIN

Britain plans to approve a ban on social media for under-16s by Christmas, with the measure set to take effect around Spring 2027, ⁠former Prime Minister Keir Starmer said on June 15.

Big tech firms operating in Britain must stop children circulating nude images on their phones or they will face legislation forcing them to do so, Starmer said on June 8.

Under the plans, firms like Apple and Google would have to build or activate technical solutions on smartphones and tablets to detect and block nude images for children. Adults would still be able to take, share or view nude content through an age verification process.

CHINA

China's cyberspace regulator has put in place a so-called "minor mode" programme that requires device-level restrictions and app-specific rules to restrict screen time depending on age.

DENMARK

Denmark said in November it would ban social media for children under 15, while parents could provide ⁠access to certain platforms to kids down to the age of 13.

FRANCE

France's top court on August 14 blocked a ​bill banning social ⁠media access for under-15s, saying it infringed upon freedom of expression.

France's parliamenthad approved the ban in July amid growing concerns about online bullying and mental health risks.

GERMANY

Minors aged 13 to 16 are allowed to use social media only if their parents provide consent. Child protection advocates say controls are insufficient.

GREECE

Greece is "very close" to announcing a social media ban for children under 15, a senior ⁠government source told Reuters on February 3.

INDIA

India's chief economic adviser called for age restrictions on social media platforms in January, describing them as "predatory" in how they keep users engaged online, two days after ​tourist state Goa said ⁠it was weighing restrictions akin to Australia's.

ITALY

Children under 14 need parental consent to ‌

MALAYSIA

Malaysia has begun barring those under 16 from registering accounts on social media platforms, its communications regulator said on June 1.

NORWAY

The Norwegian government in 2024 proposed raising the age at which children can consent to the terms required to use social media to 15 from 13, although parents would still be permitted to sign off on their behalf if ‌they are under the age limit.

The government has also begun work on legislation to set an absolute minimum age limit of ‌15 for social media use.

POLAND

Poland's ruling party is preparing new legislation to ban social media for children under 15 and to hold platforms responsible for age verification, it said on February 27.

SLOVENIA

Slovenia is drafting a law that would prohibit children under 15 from accessing social media, Deputy Prime Minister Matej Arcon said on February 6.

SPAIN

Spain will push ahead with new rules to make social networks and AI safer despite intense lobbying from the tech industry, Digital Transformation Minister Oscar Lopez told Reuters in May.

Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez had said in February that ⁠Spain would ban access to social media for minors under 16, with platforms required to implement age verification systems.

SWEDEN

Sweden should introduce a minimum age of 15 for the use of social media, a government-appointed commission recommended on June 2.

A ban can be formulated in a way that the platforms would be responsible for age verification, investigator Lisa Englund Krafft told a news conference with Social Affairs and Public Health Minister Jakob Forssmed.

TURKEY

Turkey's parliament on April 24 passed legislation banning the use of social media by children under 15 and introducing new rules for digital platforms, including game software companies.

UNITED ARAB EMIRATES

The United Arab Emirates on June 18 approved a resolution setting the minimum age for social media use at 15, the government's media office said, making it the first Arab country to introduce such a measure.

The resolution prohibits children under 15 from creating or using personal social media accounts and restricts their access to the platforms' full features.

UNITED STATES

U.S. legislation aimed at forcing social media companies to do more to protect children and teenagers cleared a key political hurdle after Republican Senator Ted Cruz ‌said on May 12 he would support the bill.

Cruz said at an event in Washington that he would back the Kids Online Safety Act, which would require social media companies to "exercise reasonable ​care" in designing features that contribute to harm to minors, according to the bill.

The legislation is separate from the long-standing Children's Online Privacy Protection Act, which prevents companies from collecting personal data ‌from children under 13 without parental consent. Several states have passed laws requiring parental consent for minors ⁠to access social media, but they have faced court challenges on free speech grounds.

EU LEGISLATION

On May 12, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the European Union would seek stronger ⁠protections for children from harmful social media features.

Von der Leyen said the Commission would target "addictive and harmful design practices" in its Digital Fairness Act, a planned law due to be proposed later this year, while an expert panel prepares advice on how to proceed.

The European Parliament ‌in November agreed on a resolution calling for an EU-wide ban ​on access for children under 16 to online platforms, video-sharing sites and AI companions without parental consent and an ‌outright ban for those younger than 13.

News.title: Top UK scientist steps down from WHO
News.content:
Sir Jeremy was promoted to Assistant Director-General in May 2025, as part of a broader leadership shake-up. He originally joined the WHO as Chief Scientist in 2023, after almost a decade at the Wellcome Trust.

Along with Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the Director-General, and others, Sir Jeremy was closely involved in implementing a painful downsizing of the WHO following the departure of the United States.

Historically, the US has been the agency’s top donor and the funding cuts have hit the agency hard.

It has committed to slashing nearly a quarter of the global workforce and shrinking the headquarters in Geneva and, under a new organisational structure, 10 divisions were merged into just four.

Sir Jeremy was responsible for one of these: Health Promotion, Disease Prevention and Control.

Speaking in March, he said: “2025 was a very difficult year. When you imagine any organisation – public or private – reducing its workforce by 30 per cent, it is extremely painful. Many institutions usually do this gradually: 10 per cent one year, another 10 per cent the next. Doing it all in a single year was awful, and the organisation lost many good people. Human resources did their best.

“I participated in the architectural overhaul and organisational redesign of WHO,” he added in an interview with the Swiss daily, Le Temps. “It is far from perfect, but the reform we have undertaken is as strategic as possible to ensure the organisation is better adapted to the health challenges of the next 20 years.”

While Sir Jeremy’s position at the WHO was a senior posting, working at the WHO, like other parts of the UN, can be frustrating, owing to its structure and governance.

The WHO is beholden to member states and is subject to enormous pressure at the international level, which determines its funding stability, influences outbreak investigations, and tests its ability to act on issues that require consensus, such as the pandemic treaty.

But it is also riven by its own internal politics, and at the moment several senior officials, including several regional directors, have stepped back from their roles to campaign for Dr Tedros’s job as head of the organisation. His second and final term as Director-General will end on August 15 next year.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football: five key budget enablers
News.content:
As the new Telegraph Fantasy Football season approaches, the fantasy football experts at Fantasy Football Hub will continue to bring you the very best in fantasy football knowledge, tips and tools to help you rise up the ranks and win your mini-leagues.

To join the Hub and get access to all their great resources and expert tips you can take advantage of its 50% pre-season discount here.

Telegraph Fantasy Football managers need to make compromises to fit in fantasy heavyweights like Erling Haaland (£8.3m) and Bruno Fernandes (6.5m). Picking some set-and-forget budget enablers who have either high point ceiling potential or will return a steady stream of points, is key to freeing up those funds.

Below are five players the Fantasy Football Hub experts have highlighted for consideration.





Brian Brobbey (£3.3m)

The Sunderland forward had a steady Premier League debut season, netting seven times and helping the Black Cats qualify for the Europa League. The Dutch international netted three times at the World Cup, improving his stock further, and will be looking to get off to a goal-scoring start against Ipswich and Fulham in GWs 1 and 2.



Enzo Le Fee (£3.3m)

Depending on the formation TFF managers are using, Brobbey’s midfield teammate at the same price may be the preferred route to target those opening fixtures. The 26-year-old accrued 12 attacking returns last season, and bumped up his overall score with an impressive 93 tackles.



Harry Wilson (£3.2m)

The midfielder swapped London for Yorkshire in the summer, as he looks to expand on a whopping 17 attacking returns from last season. Feeding the rejuvenated Dominic Calvert-Lewin (£3.9m), and adding goals from midfield for Leeds will be two primary objectives for the Welsh international, who could make a mockery of his mere marginal price increase.



James Trafford (£3.0m)

Another Leeds United summer acquisition, Daniel Farke fought off rival Premier League suitors to land the ex-Manchester City shot-stopper. Leeds United have a mixed bag in terms of opening fixture difficulty, but do have three home league games in the first five before the international break, and the new no.1 has an outside chance of getting the nod in the Carabao Cup games too, so there are points available should the Whites be able to shut out the opposition.



James Hill (£2.6m)

If looking to fit in more big-hitters, a sub £3m player can be extremely useful for team balance, and the Bournemouth defender looks assured of starting having played a pivotal role in getting the Cherries into Europe this season.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football: five essential players for the 2026/27 season
News.content:
As the new Telegraph Fantasy Football season approaches the fantasy football experts at Fantasy Football Hub, will continue to bring you the very best in fantasy football knowledge, tips and tools to help you rise up the ranks and win your mini-leagues.

To join the Hub and get access to all their great resources and expert tips you can take advantage of its 50% pre-season discount.

Five best fantasy football players





Take a look at these elite Telegraph Fantasy Football tips below:



Erling Haaland (£8.3m)

Comfortably last season’s top points scorer with 254, the Norwegian striker will once again likely be the first name in TFF Managers’ XIs. Having come back late from his post-World Cup break, there may be nervousness about early-season minutes. However, if he keeps up his phenomenal August goals-to-games ratio, starting without him may mean playing catch-up against the field.



João Pedro (£5.1m)

Having missed out on the Brazilian squad for the World Cup, the forward looks rejuvenated after a rested summer, netting seven times and assisting twice more in pre-season. With no European distractions for the Blues this season, and attacking intent shown in new manager Xabi Alonso’s selections thus far, the 24-year-old looks primed for a successful season.



Antoine Semenyo (£4.9m)

Perhaps one of the biggest surprises in the pricing for the new season was the City winger’s sub-£5m tag. The January recruit was the second-highest scorer in the game last season, and has looked the most dangerous of Enzo Moresca’s attacking assets in pre-season, so looks the stand-out midfield option.



Gabriel Magalhães (£4.9m)

Another that perhaps warranted a higher price increase, the Brazilian only missed out on breaking the 200-point barrier due to his injury late in the season. While there are cheaper options in the champions’ backline, including Christhian Mosquera (£3.7m), who looks likely to deputise for the injured William Saliba (£4.6m), getting the assurances over long-term starts and the additional attacking returns is enough to warrant paying the higher expense.



Nico O’Reilly (£4.2m)

The England international has incurred a position change in TFF, and will now gain points for clean sheets as a defender on top of his attacking returns. Had he scored as a defender last season, he would have topped his position table; therefore, £4.2m seems too good value to turn down.



One notable omission from the list is Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes (£6.5m). It isn’t through the belief that the veteran won’t return heavily once again this season, but rather that there appears to be more value across a wide range of mid-priced options where TFF managers can optimise value across their starting XIs.

News.title: Rabies deaths are rising. What is going wrong?
News.content:
In a packed intensive care ward in Dhaka, three-year-old Abdul lay paralysed, his tiny body contorted by a rabies infection that had reached his brain.

His mother, Sheuli Akter, 38, sat at his side massaging his legs in the hope that this might loosen his muscles, but it was having no effect. Even his hands and feet were seized up by cramps.

Abdul had been in the hospital for a month but doctors said he was unlikely to live much longer. The infection, they said, had progressed to degenerative encephalitis; the virus had got to his brain.

Abdul was shaking, gripped by fever. His breathing was rapid and panicked, punctuated occasionally by groans of pain.

On his chin was the telltale scar of a dog bite, the source of the infection.

“He was playing outside with the other children,” said Sheuli. “The dog, which was one of those always waiting around outside, suddenly attacked him. They said it went for him because he was the smallest.”

News.title: Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City
News.content:
Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the new signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

How about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

So what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

Title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

First Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

News.title: Rashford returns and Fernandes misses another penalty as Man Utd humbled by Amorim
News.content:
Manchester United 2 AC Milan 4

Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

News.title: Newcastle kit fiasco sums up haphazard pre-season
News.content:
Newcastle United 1 Bayer Leverkusen 2

Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.

The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.

During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.

Newcastle would go on to lose the game 2-1 in new manager Matthias Jaissle’s first game at St James’, a result which followed a 3-1 reverse against Everton on Wednesday evening.

Leverkusen, the 2023-24 Bundesliga champions now managed by Spaniard Carles Martínez Novell, scored after just 44 seconds through a powerful Ibrahim Maza strike.

News.title: Raul Jimenez’s late penalty seals share of spoils for Wolves against Blackburn
News.content:
Cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

Peixoto said: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

“We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

“We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”

Mowbray: It feels like a defeat

Tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

Mowbray said: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

“Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we showed there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”

The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

However, Wolves scored the first goal of the new campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

Sports.title: Arsenal could offer Brighton five players to beat Man Utd to statement signing
Sports.content:
Arsenal could offer Brighton five players to beat Man Utd to statement signing

Arsenal are continuing their business in the summer transfer window ahead of the Premier League season beginning

View 6 Images Mikel Arteta could offload a number of players to land the Brighton midfielder (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Arsenal could offer five players to Brighton to land Jack Hinshelwood. Mikel Arteta still aims to add to his squad after spending around £144million so far this summer.

‌



The Gunners boss plans to bring in more transfers ahead of their Premier League opener against Coventry City. Hinshelwood is one of Arsenal's primary targets and the club could consider swap deals to facilitate the move.

‌



Club officials have reportedly contacted the midfielder's representatives, with an official bid ready to be made. However, Manchester United are also keen on Hinshelwood so Arsenal may need to make their offer more attractive to Brighton.

‌



Player swaps have become something of a trend this summer following Dwight McNeil and Brennan Johnson's switch between Everton and Crystal Palace. McNeil headed south to join the Eagles while Johnson arrived on Merseyside to work under David Moyes.

The Gunners may take inspiration from this deal and offer Brighton some of their own squad to land Hinshelwood. Here, Mirror Football has looked at who Arsenal could put forward in a swap deal with the Seagulls to reduce the £51m asking price.

Gabriel Jesus

Gabriel Jesus is one of the most likely options given Brighton's desire for a centre-forward and Arsenal's openness to letting him go. The Brazilian was omitted from the Gunners' Community Shield squad at the weekend and has been heavily linked with a move.

‌



View 6 Images Gabriel Jesus could be the next departure for Arteta (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

Serie A side Napoli have registered an interest with Arsenal keen to get rid of Jesus' £265,000-a-week wages. Brighton are in the market for a striker following Danny Welbeck's move to Chelsea and could consider the 29-year-old.

Myles Lewis-Skelly

Myles Lewis-Skelly was a standout performer in Sunday's 3-0 win over Manchester City, assisting Riccardo Calafiori's superb strike in the 23rd second. The versatile star has been heavily involved throughout Arsenal's pre-season tour but has been linked with a move away from north London.

‌



View 6 Images Myles Lewis-Skelly has been touted with an exit (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

The England international was offered to Chelsea and Manchester United earlier this window. If Arsenal still want him off the books then he could be used in a deal with Brighton.

Lewis-Skelly's potential is still sky high, given his youth, and the 19-year-old can play across the middle of the park as well as both full-back positions.

‌



Ethan Nwaneri

View 6 Images Ethan Nwaneri is likely to depart north London this summer (Image: Alex Pantling/Getty Images)

Ethan Nwaneri's departure remains likely this summer after ending up on loan to Marseille last season. The 19-year-old is under contract until 2030 and the Gunners may be leaning more towards another temporary move.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola transfer moves one step closer as reason for U-turn emerges
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola transfer moves one step closer as reason for U-turn emerges

Liverpool could be edging closer to sealing a deal for Paris Saint-Germain attacker Bradley Barcola

View 3 Images Bradley Barcola is a target for Liverpool this summer (Image: Adam Davy/PA Wire)

Liverpool fans caught a glimpse of how their side under Andoni Iraola will look at the weekend. The Reds' 2-0 win over Como on Sunday saw defenders Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo make their debut for the club in an experienced first XI.

‌



However, there will be hope amongst the Anfield faithful that there's a space yet in Iraola's first XI to be filled by PSG winger Bradley Barcola. The Reds have been trailing the attacking star for months, hoping to get a deal over the line before the transfer deadline passes on September 1.

‌



Today's news sees one of the biggest transfer sagas of this summer take a twist with PSG readjusting their stance on the £145million fee they're said to be asking for the 23-year-old French international. Elsewhere, the details surrounding a failed transfer of a current Liverpool star have emerged.

‌



Transfer moves step closer

PSG are reportedly open to offers below their original valuation for Barcola this summer. French publication Jeunes Footeux claims that the European champions are offering a "discount" on the rate, after initially demanding around £145m for the winger.

The outlet says the Parisian giants are now happy to play ball with the Reds for a fee between £110m and £120m. PSG reportedly view the compromise as a "small gesture" that will encourage Liverpool to step up their pursuit of Barcola.

Fabrizio Romano also gave Reds fans an update. He believes a deal to take Barcola to Liverpool will now “accelerate” with Liverpool “pushing” to get it over the line.

‌



Transfer U-turn explained

Further details have surfaced regarding Juventus' failed pursuit of Reds shot stopper Alisson earlier this summer. The Serie A giants made an early move to try and snag the Liverpool No. 1, but their opening offer wasn't considered remotely suitable.

Alisson, 33, reportedly agreed on personal terms to move to the Bianconeri, but Liverpool have chosen to keep him for at least one more year after extending his contract.

Reporter Gianluca Di Marzio has added more information. On his podcast, he claimed Juve's first target was Alisson and the player and Italian club "had already reached an agreement."

‌



View 3 Images Alisson Becker is staying at Liverpool for another season (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

Martinez is now in limbo as Villa are on the verge of signing Japan keeper Zion Suzuki from Parma while Tottenham's Guglielmo Vicario is heading to Turin on loan instead. Alisson featured for the Reds on Sunday in their win over Como and he reaffirmed his commitment this season, claiming he is ready for the Iraola era to get underway.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Viktor Gyokores transfer offer as Premier League clubs eye Gunners star
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Viktor Gyokores transfer offer as Premier League clubs eye Gunners star

Arsenal are expected to make a huge sale shortly

View 2 Images Barcelona are reportedly preparing an offer for Viktor Gyokeres (Image: Getty )

Arsenal fans should hang on tight as the final two weeks of the summer transfer window are set to be an exhilarating ride. The Gunners showed that they are once more the favourites to lift the Premier League title this season by comprehensively beating Manchester City 3-0 in the Community Shield on Sunday.

‌



Their display showed how shrewd their summer signings have been, despite being rather understated compared to some of their rivals. Christos Tzolis and Bruno Guimaraes both started the fixture and impressed.

‌



More transfer activity in the form of new arrivals is expected before the window closes on September 1, with Mikel Arteta still wanting a versatile defender to fill in for the injured William Saliba, as well as a world-class forward.

‌



But sporting director Andrea Berta deems it necessary to first offload several players in order to raise funds and free up squad space. With Leandro Trossard being the only major departure of the summer, the north Londoners are set to ramp up their dealings over potential exits before turning their attention back to signing players.

Here, Mirror Football takes a look at the latest transfer developments concerning the Premier League champions.

‌



Gyokeres offer 'imminent'

Spanish outlet Sport has reported that Barcelona are preparing to make an offer for Arsenal’s Viktor Gyokeres 'imminently'. The La Liga champions are searching for a forward to replace Ferran Torres after the World Cup winner joined Paris Saint-Germain for £43m.

Barcelona’s first choice target is Julian Alvarez - also admired at Arsenal - but Atletico Madrid are refusing to sell the Argentine to a direct rival. As such, Barca have reportedly turned their attention to Gyokeres.

The report claimed that Barcelona would test the waters at the Emirates Stadium and "make movements in the next few hours". The Swede joined Arsenal last summer in a deal worth up to £64m and was tipped to finally end Arteta’s long search for a goal-scoring No.9.

‌



But despite scoring 21 goals in all competitions in his first campaign for the Gunners, Gyokeres’ all-around play left a lot to be desired and he often went missing in important games. That led to rumours of his potential exit earlier this summer, with previous reports claiming Arsenal were willing to offer Gyokeres in a player-plus-cash deal for Alvarez.

Rivals circling for Nwaneri

View 2 Images Ethan Nwaneri is likely to depart north London this summer (Image: Alex Pantling/Getty Images)

‌



Fabrizio Romano dropped a bombshell during Arsenal’s win over City on Sunday by claiming the decision has already been made for Ethan Nwaneri to leave the Gunners in the next two weeks. He wrote on X that the club made the decision weeks ago to let the 19-year-old, who was sent out on loan for the second half of last season, depart.

That came after Nwaneri did not even make the bench for the Community Shield clash. The versatile youngster was seen watching on from the sidelines with Gabriel Martinelli, another player heavily linked with a move away this summer, as their team-mates took part in the Principality Stadium trophy celebrations

Romano has since doubled down by claiming several clubs have already approached Arsenal over a possible deal for Nwaneri, including AC Milan, Galatasaray and unnamed German sides. He went on to say on his YouTube channel that there is a feeling at Arsenal that Premier League clubs are now expected to join the race for his signature.

Article continues below

Nwaneri is said to be conferring with his agents and family before making a decision regarding his next move following a poor loan stint with Marseille last term.

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola admits he 'loves' ex-wife Cristina but they 'lost passion'
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola admits he 'loves' ex-wife Cristina but they 'lost passion'

Pep Guardiola is the subject of a new Prime Video documentary which shows his extraordinary love for the game and his ex-wife as well as some incredible moments of man management

View 4 Images Pep kissing his ex-wife at the 2023 Champions League Final (Image: Getty Images)

Pep Guardiola believes it will be “difficult" to manage another football team after Manchester City, as the job was so demanding that it impacted his family life and has left him exhausted.

In his first interview since leaving the job after 10 years and 20 trophies, Guardiola admitted he quit feeling tired and with issues to address following the separation with his wife Cristina Serra at the end of 2024. He told his players the reason for their split was that they "lost the passion".

Looking ahead, Guardiola, 55, said: “I don't even know myself what I'm going to do, honestly. But for sure I will not be…it will be difficult to come back. That’s my feeling today. It will be difficult to come back.

‌



View 4 Images Pep in the dressing room giving a team talk (Image: Manchester City FC)

"I need to refresh many things that happened in my personal life. And professional, what I’ve found, I need to find myself a little bit in different things. Especially sitting and seeing the time go by. Or the time cross in front of you.”

He then said: “There is a word in Catalonia, it’s called ‘badar’,” and sat back looking zoned out and relaxed. Badar means to sit like this right? So I’ll do that. That is one of the main targets I want to do.” He added: “Life is not just football right? It should be sleep until 10 one day. And go to the cafeteria or take two days off. Walk? I dunno, do whatever you want. I don’t have time to read, to watch series, to travel, it’s too much to be honest.”

The interview is part of a new four-part Prime Video documentary - A Beautiful Obsession - about his final two seasons in charge of the club and the incredible impact he had in Manchester. It features some extraordinary scenes in the dressing room, where Guardiola at times instigated hugging sessions before matches to help bond with the players, but would also criticise them angrily when things went badly wrong and admit they left him feeling “so f**king tired” in defeat he sometimes wanted to kill them.

Guardiola even mentioned his marriage breakdown in one bizarre team talk to try to inspire them. In December 2024 when they lost 2-0 to Juventus in the Champions League, Pep is shown in the dressing room saying: “Guys, I want to confess something. I'm f***ing divorced from the most beautiful woman in your planet.

“It's my wife, my ex-wife. I love her unbelievably but we lost the passion. For many reasons we lost the passion. I love her? Yeah, absolutely. She loves me? Yeah. But we lost the passion.

‌



"How you play football? Because you play or because you have something inside. What is the passion? In your life, whatever you are going to do. Do it with passion. I don’t want good players, I want players with passion.”

Spanish reports in January 2025 said Serra, who had been with Guardiola since 1994 and married since 2014, wanted to stay in Barcelona to concentrate on her fashion business. But the pair, who have three children, are still on friendly terms. Former Barcelona player and coach Guardiola was furious in the dressing room a year later - and floated the idea of City getting a new manager to the players - when the club lost 2-0 to Bayer Leverkusen in a Champions League the following season in November 2025.

The match had seen him make 10 changes and give some players on the fringes of the team a starting place. But he was close to tears at the defeat, seemingly blaming himself but also the lack of courage and commitment of the squad players to step up and perform.

‌



He said: “Maybe I should apologise for the fact I made ten substitutions. But it’s impossible to play football without courage. I’m going to win the game, I’m going to show this f**king b*stard manager that I am better than the other guys.

“In the end it’s a competition between each other guys. Where is the competition today? I feel sad. I feel disappointed for myself, for the incredibly stupid thing I try to do. To make you safe, to make you secure, to make you confident to do it.

“I arrive here at eight O’clock in the morning and I stay for hours and hours trying to find something to arrive here in your heart. And when I don’t get it, it’s frustrating. And you know what is going to happen? You will have another manager.”

‌



He went on to say that if he saw the players complain about one of his decisions for the rest of the season he would “f**king kill them”.

Tearfully he added: “Work harder, work better, live better. I defend you many times but it’s unacceptable. Lack of courage, passion and love. I leave my life, my divorce and my family is away and everything for all of you. And what do you give back? The f**king performance you have done, all of you.

“It’s a disgrace guys. F**king hell, I am really f**king tired. When I see that I’m exhausted, I’m drained. I want to quit. When you play like this I feel alone.”

‌



View 4 Images Pep loves to use the tactics board before the game and at half time (Image: Manchester City FC)

The intense negative comments never seemed to last long though. During other games he repeatedly told the players he loved them and how proud he was of them and would embrace them before and after games. He also cried tears of joy after success winning trophies as well as tears of despair when they lost the league to Arsenal earlier this year, but praised his squad for pushing them to the final games of the season.

On one occasion he played the players a video of their goal celebrations with the Bee Gees song ‘You Win Again’ in the background and told them to celebrate more and for longer when they scored.

‌



“The kindness and the love and the passion and everything you’re doing. Everyone is connected,” he said grinning watching the screen and singing along as the music played.

Seen by most in the game as genius, he is also shown obsessively using the tactics board and even using videos at half time from the first half of games to make small changes in pursuit of victory.

The documentary covers the final two seasons of relentless Pep’s reign at Manchester City. By this time they had won six premier league titles including four back to back, as well as the Champions League in 2023

‌



But the last two seasons were less successful, even though he won two domestic cups last season, they didn’t win the league again and were in a stage of rebuilding the team.

Manchester City fan and Oasis guitarist Noel Gallagher compares what happened to his own band and their first three smash hit albums followed by a less successful period. He said: “You could be the greatest songwriter in the f**king world. At one point, every single thing you write becomes part of the furniture.

“Then all of a sudden, you can’t write for s**t anymore. You don’t know why. You’re not doing anything different. It’s just you have your time and the world moves on.”

‌



View 4 Images Pep strived for perfection at Manchester City (Image: Amazon Prime)

At the end of his final season in charge this year, Pep is seen telling the players the reason for his exit is simple “you have to have something that I had, the energy” he adds that “deep inside I will not have anymore”.

Pep’s family were all present for his last game with Manchester City in May including his father and ex-wife and Pep said he felt “emotion for my dad, 95, being there. Cris, the most important woman of my life, and my kids being there, it was so special for me.”

‌



Those closest to him hope he will now take at least a rest before taking on a new challenge. Txiki Bergiristain who worked alongside Pep and was City’s former Director of Football, said: “I don't know what he's going to do. He needs rest and he needs to see that outside there is a life after football.

“If he meets only football people, he is going to always be on the same rollercoaster he has been living. He needs time out, really out.”

Looking back on his time at Manchester City, Guardiola seems satisfied and previously made an emotional goodbye video for fans praising them and his love of the club and the city.

‌



He said: "What I'm proud of most is the history that we leave, you know? We saw with our eyes here in front of us. And that time…it was so fun. And the people were so happy to see that team play."

Despite his apparent reluctance to return to football management, in another interview segment of the documentary, he admits it is “addictive” when you are a manager and things go well and you are watching your team performing and almost constantly winning, as he did for many seasons.

“Older managers retire and they come back and come back,” he says with a grin. “They cannot live without it.”

* A Beautiful Obsession launches on Prime Video on Wednesday August 19.

Liverpool are making progress in their efforts to sign Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye this summer, with an agreement reached with one of the PSG talents

Sports.title: Todd Boehly and Mark Walter in talks to SELL Chelsea stakes to Clearwater
Sports.content:
Todd Boehly and Mark Walter in talks to SELL Chelsea stakes to Clearwater

Chelsea's ownership model since May 2022 has been made up of a consortium including Todd Boehly and Mark Walter, but the pair are willing to strike a deal with majority shareholder Clearlake Capital

View 2 Images Todd Boehly and Mark Walter could be set to leave Chelsea (Image: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

Chelsea shareholders Todd Boehly and Mark Walter are in talks to to sell their stakes in the Premier League club to majority owner Clearlake Capital. It comes just over four years after the BlueCo consortium including Boehly, Walter and Clearlake purchased Chelsea in a deal worth £2.5billion.

They also pledged to invest a further £1.75bn into the club which has been on a tumultuous ride since their takeover. Chelsea have spent nearly £1.5bn on player transfer fees since May 2022 but haven't won either the Premier League or Champions League.

‌



A report from The Financial Times now claims that Boehly, Chelsea's chairman and co-controlling owner, and board member Walter have been in discussions to sell their respective 12.8 per cent stakes. The deal would value the club at more than £5bn.

‌



Clearlake - a private equity firm based in California - is Chelsea's majority shareholder, boasting a 61.5 per cent stake. The remaining 38.5 per cent is split equally between Walter, Boehly and 90-year-old Swiss billionaire Hansjorg Wyss.

‌



It's unknown whether Wyss also plans to cash in. The move comes two years after it emerged that Clearlake and Boehly were prepared to buy each other out.

Chelsea's ownership model has come under fierce scrutiny since the takeover. Aside from poor recruitment, six different permanent managers and disappointing results, fans have been angered by ticket prices and spoken out against BlueCo's multi-club model.

Xabi Alonso marks Chelsea's next great hope for the men's first-team, having been appointed in May following the sacking of Liam Rosenior and an interim spell for Calum McFarlane. The Blues have spent a cool £348million on signings while recouping £138m.

‌



Where will Chelsea finish this season? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 2 Images Todd Boehly and Mark Walter own 12.8 per cent of Chelsea (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

Alonso's side kick-off their season away to West London rivals Fulham next Monday. Chelsea won three of their six pre-season games, losing two and drawing the other.

‌



Two of Chelsea's most interesting signings have been Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson, the latter of whom arrived on a free transfer. Both players are 35 and 36 respectively, signalling a change of approach from BlueCo.

Speaking to Men In Blazers recently, Alonso explained: "For sure, we need to have the right balance in everything. The right balance in physicality, the right balance in talent and experience. You need to have the right balance in players you need to develop, and to develop this maturity."

Sports.title: Australia make big batting change after shock Bangladesh loss
Sports.content:
Australia have dropped opener Jake Weatherald after their shock home loss to Bangladesh but retained Marnus Labuschagne for the must-win second Test.

Weatherald is the only change in Australia's 13-man squad for the second Test in Mackay, beginning Saturday, where the hosts will look to level the two-Test series after a humbling nine-wicket defeat in Darwin.

Bangladesh's first-ever Test win in Australia put pressure on the national cricket selectors for an overhaul of their aging line-up, with Weatherald replaced by Matt Renshaw in a bid to stabilise the top order.

Weatherald was out for 23 in the first innings and did not score in the second innings of his hometown Test, leaving him averaging 20.36 in his 12 Test innings, with Renshaw a likely contender to replace him to open with Travis Head.

Image: Matt Renshaw is a regular for Australia in ODI and T20 cricket but has not played a Test since 2023

"There was some change to Jake in terms of where he lined up and his movement patterns," coach Andrew McDonald said of Weatherald. "It's always hard to critique small sample sizes on whether it holds up [at international level].

"He dragged one on and drove at one in the first innings and was dismissed; it's probably harder with that smaller sample size to say, 'Yep, that's going to hold up under pressure'. But there was some change though."

Renshaw made his debut in 2016 and played 11 Tests before being dropped in 2018, then was recalled in 2023 for three Tests, but has only played in the shorter formats for Australia since.

He averages 29.31 with one century in 14 Tests although he impressed for Queensland in the Sheffield Shield last season, scoring three centuries among his 499 runs from six matches.

Marnus Labuschagne, who scored one and 31, was retained in the squad despite averaging 25.23 from his last 42 Test innings and not making an international century in nearly three years.

Image: Marnus Labuschagne last made a Test century in July 2023

"It's easy for me to sit here and try to defend that [Labuschagne's form]," McDonald added. "But ultimately, it's 31. It's not a big score. He's lacked runs. He feels that. We feel that. We're working incredibly hard as a coaching group … we've got to get the best out of Marn as well.

"He's had a bit of a lull. He knows that he's gone to work. I think we saw some change in the way that he played, so that's good. Some of that work that he had done feels as though it's stuck up under pressure."

Australia squad: Pat Cummins (captain), Scott Boland, Alex Carey, Cameron Green, Josh Hazlewood, Travis Head, Josh Inglis, Marnus Labuschagne, Nathan Lyon, Matthew Renshaw, Steve Smith, Mitchell Starc, Beau Webster.

Sports.title: Williams sisters lose tie-break thriller in first doubles reunion since 2022
Sports.content:
Serena and Venus Williams were narrowly beaten in their first doubles match together in four years during a dramatic first-round tie-break exit at the Cincinnati Open.

The Williams sisters, a wild-card entry into the event, were beaten 2-6 6-1 10-8 by Ukrainian Marta Kostyuk and American Peyton Stearns.

The fan favourites bounced back from a rusty first set to dominate the next and force the 10-point tie-break, where the Williams sisters trailed 6-0 before rallying again to threaten a famous comeback.

Image: Serena Williams was making just her fourth appearance, in singles or doubles, of the summer

Back-to-back double-faults by Kostyuk saw the Williams sisters reduce the deficit to 8-7, before the match ended anticlimactically with a double fault from Venus Williams.

"I thought it was fun," Serena said. "I thought it was special. We kicked off a little rust in the middle of the match and just, you know [were] starting to feel it.

"I didn't come out here to win this tournament. Winning is obviously great. But in this position just, you know, having fun. It was really cool to be able to do this again."

Image: Serena Williams, left, and Venus Williams were beaten at the Cincinnati Open

The Williams sisters, who together have won 14 Grand Slam doubles titles, were due to team up for doubles at Wimbledon but had to withdraw due to Serena's injury.

The sisters' appearance together was their first since the 2022 US Open and their first in a non-Grand Slam event since the Italian Open, with the match only Serena's fourth since returning to the WTA Tour this summer aged 44.

Image: The Williams sisters narrowly missed out on a first-round victory in Cincinnati

"Eventually we would find our way to each other," the 46-year-old Venus said about the decision to play doubles again. "It's our first time playing together in forever. It was great for us to get out there and do it."

Kostyuk and Stearns are playing in their first tournament together and will now face third seeds Guo Hanyu and Kristina Mladenovic in the next round.

"The crowd got the show," Kostyuk said. "They probably couldn't ask for anything better. At the end a tie-break is a lottery. You never know which way it's going to go."

Sports.title: How can Hamilton and Ferrari turbocharge a title challenge?
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton prepares to resume the 2026 Formula 1 season as Kimi Antonelli's nearest points challenger in the Drivers' Championship, but what do the seven-time champion and the Ferrari team need to do if that mid-season position is going to translate into a full-on title push?

Antonelli's lead of 50 points is certainly an impressive one for the Mercedes youngster at the half-way point of the year but not insurmountable if one of the chasing pack behind him in the standings can string a run of strong results together with up to 12 races still to come this season.

So what do Hamilton - and potentially team-mate Charles Leclerc, who is 31 points further back - need to keep Ferrari in play for a first drivers' title in 19 years over the next three-and-a-half months, while the team aim to crank up the pressure on Mercedes in the constructors' chase too...

Cut out the mistakes

Hamilton personally made clear when F1 broke for summer in Hungary that he had one clear goal for when the season restarted.

Although he regained second place in the standings from former team-mate George Russell in the final double-header before the break, Hamilton was left frustrated by the errors - and subsequent penalties - that had started to become far too frequent for his liking.

One in-race penalty apiece at Silverstone (false start) and Spa-Francorchamps (colliding with Russell) was followed by two more in as many days in Hungary. The first came after qualifying for blocking Oscar Piastri, which the Ferrari pit wall took the blame for and which cost Hamilton a crucial front-row berth, before the race saw him penalised for pit-lane speeding.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes driver George Russell spins after contact with Lewis Hamilton and his race ends on the opening lap, but was the Ferrari driver's penalty fair?

Finishing only fifth on a weekend that had originally offered so much promise for Ferrari led a rueful Hamilton to admit that "ultimately these last few races have been costly with mistakes from myself". He described the first half of the season - which was headlined by his first Ferrari win in Spain - as having been "ok" but "not perfect from my side", before adding: "I've really got to work hard to try to figure out how I can do better in the second half."

He also resolved to "work hard to not give them [the stewards] any opportunity to give me any more penalties moving forwards".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton's P2 is under threat as Oscar Piastri was blocked during qualifying at the Hungarian Grand Prix.

While both Antonelli and Russell can point to more points lost through Mercedes unreliability than Hamilton can stewards' penalties, in a title race where the seven-time champion needs to make 50 points up from here just to be back on level terms, he cannot afford to give away any more points so cheaply for small, but costly, infringements.

Ferrari must out-develop rivals

Ultimately a sustained title challenge for either Hamilton or Leclerc will largely depend on how successfully Ferrari manage to develop the SF-26 car between now and the end of the season.

Having gone over 18 months without a race win to June, two victories in the five races before the summer break pointed to undoubted progress and Ferrari were generally the most consistent challenger to Mercedes over the first half-season of the sport's new regulations.

However, the last race in Hungary - when Lando Norris ended up producing a dominant win in an upgraded McLaren despite Ferrari having looked the team most likely to deliver that kind of front-running on Friday - underlined that they aren't the sole rivals to Mercedes for wins.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix.

So their challenge is to not only out-develop Mercedes but McLaren and Red Bull, who have shown flashes of improved form recently, too.

Team principal Frederic Vasseur said after Hungary: "The most important thing will be to be able to keep the pace in the development.

"McLaren did a good job for a while, but they don't have exactly the same philosophy because they are bringing a big package. For sure each time they bring something, they are making a huge step. We have a different approach, trying to bring parts every race.

"We have to keep this momentum because there are still 12 races to go. It's a lot. We have a room for improvement on the chassis everywhere and we have to keep this pace."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the F1 Show podcast, David Croft questions whether Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton can challenge Kimi Antonelli for this season's world championship.

Ferrari also have a second ADUO engine upgrade to deploy amid suggestions it will be a more significant than the first, which was introduced at the Austrian Grand Prix in June.

Mercedes, ranked as having the second-top engine behind Red Bull in the first ADUO assessment window, also have one upgrade to introduce this year should they wish.

Hamilton has consistently focused on the need to improve their power relative to his old team and Vasseur said: "We know that we have to improve on the engine side and we will do it. The inertia on the engine is much higher than on the chassis."

Keep points advantage over team-mate

Hamilton resumes the season with a 31-point buffer over fourth-placed Leclerc in the standings. It was a 28-point advantage in the Monegasque's favour after 11 races last year, which underlines the improvement that Hamilton has made in his second season in red despite his recent frustrations.

There were signs in the races before the break that Leclerc was finding his way with the SF-26 after a difficult run of results earlier in the summer when incidents and a lack of pace proved costly. He won at Silverstone and outqualified Hamilton in three of the four races before the break, edging him back ahead in their Saturday head-to-head.

But there was little to choose between the pair on pace still and Hamilton was the faster of the two in Hungary before his three-place grid penalty knocked him off the front row and put him on the back foot for the race.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc reflected on his 'very special' victory at Silverstone in the last race at the British Grand Prix.

Hamilton, of course, has to beat everyone if dreams of an eighth world title are to be realised this year but keeping Leclerc at arm's length in the standings could be advantageous if Ferrari really were able to take things down to the wire.

Vasseur consistently batted off presumptive and theoretical questions in the first part of the season about whether team orders might be needed later in the year if only one driver was in realistic title contention.

While it would be highly unlikely for the Scuderia to make an early call to back one over the other anytime soon, being the Ferrari driver ahead in the points the longer the season wears on could have added significance for the closing rounds.

Make experience count

How much of an advantage could be Hamilton's far greater title-contending (and winning) experience over his nearest rivals in the standings prove to be if his challenge gathers pace?

The comparison between the top two alone is certainly stark in that respect.

Antonelli, who remains a teenager for one more week, is in his second season of Formula 1 and his first with a title-challenging car.

Hamilton is 41 years old and in his 20th season on the grid. He has won a joint-record seven world titles in F1, while also being involved in three other championship fights that went down to the wire.

Even Russell, who at 28 is eight years team-mate Antonelli's senior, is in the first title-challenging season of his eight-year F1 career.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Relive what some of the Formula One drivers, including Lewis Hamilton, George Russell and Kimi Antonelli, got up to during the summer break!

Leclerc, who turns 29 in October, has also not yet experienced a season-long title challenge. Of the other world champions in front-running cars who do know what it's like to go the distance, reigning title winner Lando Norris is 91 points back on Antonelli and four-time champion Max Verstappen 110 points adrift.

So Hamilton holds a unique experience edge over the most-likely contenders, although whether that will count for much over the remainder of the season remains to be seen.

Antonelli has made few sizeable missteps this season to this point - including a stunningly faultless drive to victory around wall-lined Monaco in June - while the Italian won almost every junior championship in which he competed before F2.

Ferrari also need to be operationally fault-less

Ferrari too will likely further have to raise their game to overturn what stands as a 72-point deficit to Mercedes in the Constructors' Championship. Although, as Frederic Vasseur pointed out in Hungary, they did outscore the Silver Arrows in all three races prior to the summer break - by a total of 26 points.

Still, there is obviously room for improvement, particularly if Mercedes get on top of the unreliability that has clearly cost them a much bigger lead to this point.

On Ferrari's side, the Hungarian GP was a case in point with Hamilton left questioning his third pit stop under a Virtual Safety Car which dropped him back behind Antonelli and Max Verstappen. While he blamed himself for speeding in the pit lane, he was still right that the perhaps-unnecessary stop "opened up the door" to the infringement in the first place.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player With the Formula One season set to resume after the summer break, we look back at how Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli has built a 50-point lead in the driver standings.

Vasseur described Ferrari's whole execution of the race as "very poor", although felt it was the exception rather than the rule for the team's in a strategic sense so far this season.

"Where do we have to improve? If I draw a conclusion based on Hungary, I would say execution," he said.

"But execution so far was probably a good one for us from the beginning of the season."

Sports.title: Rugby's greatest rivalry? The history of All Blacks vs Springboks
Sports.content:
In 2026 there is no Rugby Championship, but there is a throwback-type tour which sees New Zealand's All Blacks visit South Africa for eight matches, including four Tests against the Springboks, live on Sky Sports.

It's been advertised in New Zealand and South Africa as "Rugby's Greatest Rivalry Tour." A series of games to celebrate over a century of contests between the two most successful nations the sport has seen.

The All Blacks have already played and beaten the Stormers, Sharks and Bulls so far, and face the Springboks in Tests on August 22, August 29, September 5 and September 12.

So, what is the history between the two? And what have been the flashpoints and major moments over the decades? We take a look...

New Zealand's 2026 tour of South Africa, live on Sky Sports Friday August 7: Stormers 21-38 New Zealand, Cape Town Tuesday August 11: Sharks 0-54 New Zealand, Durban Saturday August 15: Bulls 19-50 New Zealand, Pretoria Saturday August 22: South Africa vs New Zealand (FIRST TEST), Ellis Park Stadium, Johannesburg (4.10pm BST) Tuesday August 25: Lions vs New Zealand, Johannesburg (6pm BST) Saturday August 29: South Africa vs New Zealand (SECOND TEST), Cape Town (4.10pm BST) Saturday September 5: South Africa vs New Zealand (THIRD TEST), FNB Stadium, Johannesburg (4.10pm BST) Saturday September 12: South Africa vs New Zealand (FOURTH TEST), M&T Bank Stadium, Baltimore USA (10pm BST)

Image: All Blacks vs Springboks - is it rugby's greatest rivalry?

The birth of a rivalry

New Zealand and South Africa first met on August 13, 1921 in Carisbrook, Dunedin as part of South Africa's three-Test tour, with the All Blacks coming out with a 13-5 victory.

South Africa won a week later at Eden Park 9-5, with the third Test a 0-0 draw in Wellington to see the series end 1-1. And so set in motion a rugby rivalry which has endured right at the apex of the sport.

That first match included, there have been some 110 Test meetings, the All Blacks winning 63, South Africa 43 and four draws.

There have been 54 Tests played in South Africa, with the hosts winning 28, New Zealand 25 and one draw, while 48 Tests in New Zealand have seen the All Blacks win 34, Springboks 11 and three draws.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player In 2023, South Africa captain Siya Kolisi spoke about the history of their rivalry with New Zealand

At Rugby World Cups, South Africa have beaten New Zealand in two dramatic finals (1995, 2023), and in one third-place playoff (1999), while New Zealand have beaten South Africa in the 2015 semi-finals, 2003 quarter-finals and 2023 pool stages.

After that original 1921 tour, the next time the sides met came in 1927 when New Zealand toured South Africa and again, the series finished in a captivating draw: 2-2 this time with wins for the Boks in Durban and Port Elizabeth, and wins for the All Blacks in Johannesburg and Cape Town.

South Africa won the next two series between the sides, touring New Zealand in 1937 and winning 2-1, while hosting the All Blacks in 1949 and winning 4-0.

In 1956, New Zealand get their own back as they clinched a 3-1 home series success over the Springboks, though 1960 saw South Africa back to winning ways via a 2-1 series win back on home soil.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Greatest Rivalry tour match between the Bulls and New Zealand in Pretoria

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ma'a Nonu gave his former All Blacks team-mates the ultimate show of respect by responding to their haka with one of his own

South Africa's apartheid era, worldwide sporting ban and protests

Between 1948 and 1994, though, South Africa enforced apartheid, the institutionalised racial segregation and white minority rule.

As part of this shameful system, South Africa refused to allow people of different races to play sport together, with officials requesting Māori players not be involved in series between the nations. New Zealand agreed and excluded some of their finest players from several tours, with the first major public protests coming during that 1960 tour to South Africa.

By 1964, South Africa as a sporting nation were barred from participating at the Tokyo Olympic Games, and in 1970 they were formally expelled from the International Olympic Committee. They were excluded from international tennis and the Davis Cup the same year.

Throughout the rest of the 1970s, widespread cancellations and bans for South Africa in international sport continued, but rugby proved one of the last to take action.

Indeed, 1965 saw South Africa tour New Zealand with the All Blacks winning three Tests to one, before the Halt All Racist Tours protest group was established in New Zealand in 1969 to oppose continued tours to and from South Africa.

The All Blacks toured South Africa in 1970 in any case, losing 3-1 to the Springboks, and though a 1973 tour to New Zealand was cancelled amid a climate of South Africa's worldwide sporting expulsion, series between the nations still took place in 1976 and 1981 - South Africa winning the former at home 3-1, and New Zealand the latter series 2-1 which was dogged by protests and worldwide condemnation.

Indeed, during that 1981 tour two games were cancelled. One in Hamilton saw 200 protestors rip down a chain fence, sprinkle nails all over the pitch and stage a sit-in on the halfway line, while a match against South Canterbury at Timaru was cancelled because the authorities said they would not be able to control demonstrations there.

During the final Test of the tour, an aircraft continually flew overhead the pitch and dropped flour bombs, flares and leaflets in protest. All Blacks prop Gary Knight was temporarily stunned by a flour bomb.

Eventually, the planned 1985 series between the two was cancelled in line with South Africa's wider sporting ban, with a legal ruling in New Zealand determining it would be "incompatible with the NZRFU's legally stated purpose of fostering and encouragement of the game of rugby."

Image: An orange smoke bomb is thrown onto the pitch by anti-apartheid protestors during South Africa vs Barbarians

The Springboks were barred from rugby's first two World Cups in 1987 and 1991, while a 1986 British and Irish Lions tour was also cancelled.

After the 1985 series between South Africa and New Zealand was cancelled, a 'rebel tour' which was not government-sanctioned was organised, and a team travelled in 1986 called New Zealand Cavaliers. The Kiwi players involved received condemnation, were banned for several Tests after the tour and some never played for New Zealand again.

South Africa's return to international sport and contentious World Cup glory

Upon the end of the apartheid regime, South Africa organised a Test against the All Blacks in 1992 for their first encounter since being welcomed back to international sport, and even went on to surprisingly win it 27-24 at Ellis Park.

With the released Nelson Mandela inaugurated as president in 1994, he encouraged all South Africans to back the previously hated Springboks.

In 1994, South Africa toured New Zealand for the first time in nearly 20 years, losing two Tests and drawing one, with South Africa then hosting the 1995 Rugby World Cup.

Ranked ninth in the world after their lengthy period of sporting exile, South Africa shocked many by progressing to the final where Jonah Lomu and the All Blacks awaited.

A fairytale 15-12 World Cup final victory over New Zealand at Ellis Park followed, but was there foul play involved?

Image: South Africa shocked the world by returning to international sport and winning the 1995 World Cup on home soil

The All Blacks had outscored their opponents 315-104 en route to the final, and were heavy, heavy favourites, yet they failed to score a single try in a contest that went through extra- time. How?

For many, the reason lies with the fact that a hefty proportion of the New Zealand team were struck down by illness or food poisoning on the cusp of the final.

For All Blacks head coach at the time, Laurie Mains, the culprit was a disappearing waitress named 'Suzie' - a conspiracy theory that was never proven, though Mains even hired a private investigator after the final. Team doctor Mike Bowen has also always insisted the All Blacks were poisoned, as has South African security guard Rory Steyn.

Image: Nelson Mandela handing Springboks captain Francois Pienaar the 1995 Rugby World Cup trophy in South Africa is one of sport's most famous images

What is indisputable is that a large majority of the All Blacks squad were struck down with violent illness in the days before a World Cup final against the Springboks in South Africa.

Image: Jonah Lomu and New Zealand were huge favourites for the 1995 World Cup final, but the squad were struck down with violent illness

New Zealand's 'Incomparables' and period of dominance

A little over a year after that World Cup final, the All Blacks toured South Africa in August 1996 set on revenge.

They had already beaten the Springboks home and away during the inaugural 1996 Tri-Nations, clinching the title, but a three-Test tour in South Africa against the world champions was built up as the next major challenge.

In New Zealand, that side are now known as 'The Incomparables,' as they played some magnificent rugby to launch rugby's era of professionalism, winning the first Test 23-19 in Durban, and then the second Test 33-26 at Loftus Versfeld in Pretoria, clinching the series with a Test to spare.

South Africa won that third Test, but it mattered little as the All Blacks kicked on to win 13 of the next 17 contests - going unbeaten against the Boks between 2001 and July 2004. Tri-Nations titles followed in 1997, 1999, 2002 and 2003.

Image: New Zealand's 2015 Rugby World Cup winners, including likes of Richie McCaw and Dan Carter, are widely considered the greatest side ever

The Springboks landed Tri-Nations titles in 2004 and 2009, but outside of those years, New Zealand firmly established themselves as the premier nation on the globe.

The All Blacks won Tri-Nations titles four years in a row between 2005 and 2008, again in 2010, then three more years in a row between 2011 and 2013, and three more years in a row again between 2016 and 2018. They also lifted Rugby World Cup titles in 2011 and 2015 - the latter with a side many consider the greatest ever.

They were caught by France at the 2007 World Cup despite being huge favourites, as South Africa went on to lift their second Webb Ellis Trophy, but the Boks failed to clinch silverware in any form between 2009 and 2019.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Greatest Rivalry tour match between the Stormers and New Zealand

A recent shift in South Africa's favour

September 16, 2017 proved one of South Africa's darkest rugby days, when they travelled to Albany and were defeated 57-0 by the All Blacks.

They were beaten by Ireland 38-3 in Dublin two months later, losing to Wales in Cardiff the same Test window. Such form followed a 2016 in which the Springboks were soundly beaten by England and Wales, lost to Italy for the first time, were beaten by Argentina and Australia, lost to Ireland at home and went down 57-15 to the All Blacks.

Enough was enough, and so heralded the era of Rassie Erasmus.

The controversial, unusual rugby head coach of the Springboks totally turned around South Africa's fortunes.

Image: Rassie Erasmus totally changed the fortunes of the Springboks when taking charge in 2018

By September 2018, a rejuvenated, confident side travelled to New Zealand and picked up a shock 36-34 victory in Wellington - a first win on Kiwi soil since 2009.

A little over a year later, South Africa became world champions for the third time, clinching World Cup glory vs England in the final in Japan - Eddie Jones' side having dealt with the All Blacks in the semi-finals, after the latter had beaten South Africa during the pool stages.

Image: South Africa clinched Rugby World Cup glory for the third time in 2019, despite New Zealand earlier beating them during the pool stages

Since that tournament, in 11 Tests between South Africa and New Zealand, the Springboks have won seven of them, winning Rugby Championship crowns in 2024 and 2025, and the 2023 Rugby World Cup final - albeit the latter victory came in fortunate fashion, it must be said, against a 14-player All Blacks side who probably deserved victory.

Image: The Springboks narrowly beat New Zealand to win the 2023 Rugby World Cup final in Paris

If the 2023 South Africa side was strong, the current one is likely even better, with greater depth, while the All Blacks are looking to rebuild again under Dave Rennie, with Scott Robertson having been sacked.

"With eight matches in six weeks, including a four-Test series against the Springboks, this would have to be the toughest tour in rugby," Rennie said.

"It will be an intense seven weeks of touring but an excellent opportunity for us to pit ourselves against the current benchmark team in world rugby, and to build connections with each other in a way that only a tour of this scale can do."

Tuesday August 11: Sharks 0-54 New Zealand, Durban

Saturday August 15: Bulls 19-50 New Zealand, Pretoria

Saturday August 22: South Africa vs New Zealand (FIRST TEST), Ellis Park Stadium, Johannesburg (4.10pm BST)
