Limburg brewery Alfa has won one of the top prizes at the World Beer Awards for the second time.

The family firm, based in Thull, was awarded the title of World’s Best Classic Pilsener for Edel Pils, which previously won the honour in 2021.

It was one of four Dutch beers to win a Gold award at the annual festival in the English city of Norwich, along with Grolsch’s Cal and Herfstbok and the Gouverneur Superieur Pilsener made by another Limburg brewery, Lindeboom.

Edel Pils was also named as the best Dutch national beer by the international jury.

Alfa has been brewing beer in Thull for 156 years, using traditional family recipes and its own water source.

World.title: Dutch companies to receive €1bn in Trump tariff compensation
World.content:
Dutch companies are set to recoup a €1 billion windfall from the Trump administration after the United States Supreme Court ruled most of his “liberation day” tariffs announced last April were illegal.

Philips, one of the first companies to claim a refund following the ruling in February, received €186 mln, which accounted for around 4% of its turnover for the second quarter of 2026.

The figures were included in the health tech giant’s latest quarterly results, which showed a 4% increase in sales compared to the same period in 2025.

The Supreme Court ordered the US government to compensate companies when it upheld a lower court’s decision that the Trump administration had wrongly used emergency powers to justify the tariffs.

Exactly how much has been paid out is unknown because the government has not published details, but experts have calculated that the top 10 Dutch exporters stand to receive more than €1 bn altogether.

Philips, which makes 40% of its turnover in North America, was one of the first Dutch companies to claim a refund. Other major exporters include Heineken, which is expected to receive between €150 mln and €350 mln, and Ahold Delaize, owner of Albert Heijn, which will get an estimated €100 mln to €300 million.

Altogether more than a quarter of a million companies have claimed refunds worth a total of $129 bn (€111 bn) from the US customs administration, in addition to the $166 bn (€143 bn) which will have to be repaid to American firms.

“We are surprised by how quickly and efficiently this has happened,” Casper Roerade of Dutch entrepreneurs’ association EvoFenedex told AD.nl.

World.title: Twelve killed as Polish coach crashes in Hungary
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Twelve people have died after a bus carrying Polish pilgrims from Medjugorje in Bosnia and Herzegovina back to Poland crashed on a motorway in Hungary. Initial findings indicate that the cause of the accident was the driver of the coach falling asleep. Political leaders in both Poland and Hungary have offered condolences to the families of the victims, while the Polish foreign ministry has set up a special helpline for those affected. BREAKING: 12 people have been killed after a Polish tourist bus crashed on a motorway in Hungary https://t.co/PAiZ4D1jU3 📺 Sky 501, Virgin 602, Freeview 233 and YouTube pic.twitter.com/yxW9tBN5bw — Sky News (@SkyNews) August 16, 2026 The accident occurred at around 1 a.m. local time on the night of Saturday to Sunday on the M3 motorway in Hungary. Later on Sunday morning, Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar confirmed that 12 people had died and at least 10 were seriously injured. According to information from the Hungarian emergency services, 57 passengers and two drivers had been on the bus. “The driver probably fell asleep at the wheel”, resulting in the vehicle veering off the road and into a ditch, said police in a statement quoted by Polsat News. Polsat reports that the group is from around Strzyżów, a town in southeastern Poland. The owner of the local company that had been transporting them told Business Insider Polska that the coach “was driven by two experienced drivers”. Twelve people lost their lives and at least ten were seriously injured overnight when a bus carrying Polish tourists overturned and went off the road into a ditch on the M3 motorway. My sincere condolences to the families of the victims. I am grateful to all those who took part… — Magyar Péter (Ne féljetek) (@magyarpeterMP) August 16, 2026 Polish media outlets reported that the group in the bus were pilgrims on their way back to Poland from Medjugorje, which is a popular destination for Catholic pilgrimages due to a series of reported visions of the Virgin Mary that have occurred there. Polish foreign ministry spokesman Maciej Wewiór later confirmed to broadcaster TVN that “everything indicates they were returning from Medjugorje”. The authorities in Podkarpackie, the province of Poland where the group was from, also reported that they were pilgrims returning from Bosnia and Herzegovina. The accident on Sunday morning took place just after the end of celebrations of the Assumption of Mary on Saturday, which had included the unveiling in Poland of Europe’s tallest statue of Mary. Poland’s president, Karol Nawrocki, issued a statement on Sunday morning expressing his “deep sorrow…in the face of this unimaginable tragedy” and offering “prayer and profound compassion for the families and loved ones of the victims”. Prime Minister Donald Tusk likewise expressed his “deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of the victims” and thanked the Hungarian emergency services for undertaking the rescue operation. Andrii Sybiha, the foreign minister of Ukraine, which borders both Poland and Hungary, also offered his “heartfelt condolences” and said that “Ukraine stands in solidarity with the friendly Polish people and shares their grief”. The Polish embassy in Budapest has set up a special helpline for family members and loved ones of those involved in the crash. World.title: Europe’s biggest Virgin Mary statue – taller than Rio’s Christ the Redeemer – unveiled in Polish village
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The tallest statue of the Virgin Mary in Europe has been officially opened in the small village of Konotopie in central Poland. Towering over the rural landscape at 55.6 metres high, the monument, whose construction was funded by a wealthy local couple, is taller than the famous Christ the Redeemer statue in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The new landmark, which is also the tallest religious statue of any kind in Europe, was unveiled on 15 August, when Catholics celebrate the assumption of Mary into heaven. The consecration ceremony was led by Krzysztof Wętkowski, bishop of the diocese of Włocławek in which Konotopie, which has a population of only around 130 people, is located. The local community hopes that the statue will become a major site of pilgrimage. Among those to attend the ceremony was former Polish president and Nobel Peace Prize winner Lech Wałęsa. “We sinners ask Our Lady of Mercy to take care of the whole nation,” wrote the 82-year-old in a post on social media, sharing photos of himself at the statue. Construction of the concrete statue took 18 months and reportedly cost around 100 million zloty (€23.2 million). Those costs were covered by the couple behind the project, Roman and Grażyna Karkosik. After making his fortune investing in undervalued companies during Poland’s post-communist transition in the 1990s, Roman Karkosik had by the early 21st century become one of Poland’s richest people, though his fortune has since diminished somewhat, according to estimates. The couple – who keep an extremely low profile, rarely giving interviews and never speaking publicly about the project to build the statue of Mary – live in a restored 18th-century palace around 2 kilometres away, from where they can see the new monument. Konotopie’s statue of Mary has now overtaken one in Miribel, France, as Europe’s tallest. But it is still some distance behind the tallest in the world, the 98-metre Mother of All Asia–Tower of Peace in Batangas City, Philippines. Until recently, Poland also had the tallest statue of Jesus in the world, the 33-metre-high Jesus Christ the King of the Universe monument, erected in the town of Świebodzin in 2010. However, in 2024, it was overtaken by a 61-metre-tall statue of Jesus in Indonesia. The design for the statue of Mary in Konotopie was originally conceived in the form of a two-metre-high model by sculptor Adam Jakub Matejkowski, who told the Polish edition of Forbes magazine that the Karkosiks had specifically requested that the statue be larger than Świebodzin’s Christ. Chief engineer Bartłomiej Niesłuchowski told broadcaster TVN that it took months to find a company willing and able to undertake such a project. Because no suppliers in Poland could produce the material needed for the unique mould into which the concrete would be poured, it had to be manufactured in Italy. The monument will be free for the public to access, including its observation deck, located 15 metres up on the pedestal upon which Mary stands. The site is expected to become a place of pilgrimage, with local authorities preparing for an influx of people. “We’re already seeing growing interest in investment plots, including restaurants,” Renata Gołębiewska, mayor of the nearby town of Kikoł, told the Rzeczpospolita daily. “But it’s too early to assess the impact.” Poland is one of Europe’s most religious countries. Just over 70% of the population identify as Catholic, according to the most recent national census, while around 30% attend Sunday mass. However, religiosity has been falling rapidly in recent years, especially among young Poles. The Catholic church in Poland has also been hit by a series of scandals relating to historical child sex abuse as well as accusations that it interferes in politics. The proportion of Catholics who attend Sunday mass in Poland has stabilised at around 30% after falling from a peak of 57%, new church data show. The proportion of children taking Catholic catechism in schools has continued to fall but remains a majority https://t.co/5bu35hzJ7c — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 17, 2025 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Polish opposition expels 40 lawmakers who formed breakaway caucus led by ex-PM Morawiecki
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s largest opposition party, the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), has expelled 40 of its lawmakers in response to them forming a breakaway parliamentary caucus led by PiS deputy leader and former prime minister Mateusz Morawiecki. The decision formalises a split that began last month, when Morawiecki and his supporters refused to resign from a political association they had formed and sign a pledge of loyalty to PiS. They represented a more moderate faction that had long been unhappy with the party’s move in a hard-right direction. Koleżeński Sąd Dyscyplinarny PiS podjął decyzję o wykluczeniu z partii 38 posłów i 2 senatorów wchodzących w skład klubu Rozwój Plus, w tym byłego premiera Mateusza Morawieckiego – przekazał rzecznik dyscyplinarny PiS Karol Karski. https://t.co/Qe6KuPVUVZ — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) August 13, 2026 On Thursday, PiS’s disciplinary spokesman, Karol Karski, announced that its disciplinary court had found that 38 MPs and two senators “seriously violated the PiS statute by leaving the PiS parliamentary caucus and joining a new caucus” founded by Morawiecki, called Development Plus (Rozwój Plus). Karski added that all 40, including Morawiecki, had been notified of the decision by email and been sent scans of the ruling. They have seven days to appeal. If no appeal is filed, they will officially cease to be PiS members, Karski said. A statement from the party’s disciplinary court, cited by news website Onet, also noted that Morawiecki had committed a further “serious violation” of the party’s statute by announcing last week that Development Plus would become a political party. Mateusz Morawiecki has confirmed that his Development Plus group, which is splitting from the national-conservative opposition PiS party, will soon form a party of its own. However, he categorically ruled out ever working with Prime Minister @donaldtusk https://t.co/J6mQaer4MA — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 4, 2026 Among those to be expelled are several former government ministers, including Janusz Cieszyński, Paweł Jabłoński, Olga Semeniuk-Patkowska and Szymon Szynkowski vel Sęk. Some of the ousted lawmakers expressed their disappointment at PiS’s decision. “Someone who has done everything for PiS is being expelled simply because he wanted to broaden the party’s voter base,” Grzegorz Puda, another former minister, told the Fakt daily. Another, Łukasz Schreiber, told news website Onet that, in reality, the decision to expel them had been taken when party leader Jarosław Kaczyński said in July they had effectively resigned by refusing to sign the loyalty pledge. “Everything else was just a formality.” Morawiecki served as prime minister from 2017 until 2023, when PiS lost power to the current government, a more liberal coalition led by Donald Tusk. The party has plunged into crisis this year, with its support in polls falling to the lowest level in over 15 years. In response to a growing challenge from the far right, Kaczyński has shifted PiS itself rightwards. That frustrated more moderate figures around Morawiecki, who founded the Development Plus association in April this year as a way of promoting their ideas. However, that prompted criticism from some other members of the party, who saw it as a step towards creating a breakaway group. The split in PiS is a blow to the party and its leader, Jarosław Kaczyński. But the potential emergence of a new centre-right party led by Mateusz Morawiecki could actually help the opposition win a majority at next year's elections, writes @danieltilles1 https://t.co/xMP7e4rOFf — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 31, 2026 Matters came to a head in July, when Morawiecki and his supporters refused to quit their association and sign the pledge of loyalty demanded by Kaczyński. They then formed their own caucus, which immediately became the third largest in parliament and meant that PiS’s was no longer the biggest. Last week, Morawiecki confirmed that his group would soon form a new party of its own. He laid out a vision of a more moderate, centre-right party that would focus on economic development rather than “ideological disputes”. Its first policy proposal was to establish a special “salary” for parents, equivalent to the minimum wage, that they would be paid for the first three years of a child’s life, with the aim of boosting Poland’s birth rate, which is one of the lowest in the world. According to poll aggregator eWybory.eu, Development Plus already has average support of 5.6% in polls, despite not yet being a party. Support for PiS has fallen to 20.3%, down from 24.4% in July. World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has introduced a new type of account that will allow individuals to invest up to 100,000 zloty (€23,200) without paying capital gains tax. The government says the scheme is designed to encourage Poles to build long-term savings and channel billions of zloty into the domestic financial market. Osobiste Konta Inwestycyjne to nowe narzędzie, które ułatwi inwestowanie i oszczędzanie na preferencyjnych warunkach podatkowych. Nowe przepisy wejdą w życie 1 stycznia 2027 r. Szczegóły w komunikacie ⤵️ https://t.co/Z6zEHKkQsY — Ministerstwo Finansów (@MF_GOV_PL) August 13, 2026 The new legislation, which was signed into law on Thursday by President Karol Nawrocki and will take effect on 1 January 2027, creates Personal Investment Accounts (OKI). All assets held in an OKI will be completely exempt from the usual 19% capital gains tax. Amounts up to 100,000 zloty, including up to 25,000 in savings assets such as bonds and deposits, will be completely tax free. Assets above 100,000 zloty will be subject to a new tax on their value. The government has said the tax will amount to 0.85% in 2027 and will be adjusted annually. Finance minister Andrzej Domański earlier described the introduction of OKI as “the biggest change in years for individual investors and the largest project aimed at building domestic capital to drive the development of the Polish economy”. While Nawrocki, who is aligned with the opposition, regularly clashes with the government and has vetoed a record number of laws, in this case he approved their idea, which he office said “could have a positive impact on both citizens and the state”. “Poles will gain a tool to promote family wealth building thanks to an attractive tax-free allowance and a guarantee of no account maintenance fees,” they added. Sejm przyjął ustawę o Osobistych Kontach Inwestycyjnych. Do 100 tys. zł bez podatku. To największa od lat zmiana dla indywidualnych inwestorów i największy projekt budowy krajowego kapitału napędzającego rozwój polskiej gospodarki. 🇵🇱 — Andrzej Domański (@Domanski_Andrz) July 3, 2026 The government estimates the scheme could result in about 74 billion zloty flowing to the Warsaw Stock Exchange by 2040. Kamil Gemra, an assistant professor at the Warsaw School of Economics, said he considered the projection realistic. “Society is getting wealthier; we have record amounts in our bank accounts. It would be enough for just a few per cent of that money to flow into the capital market for the figure cited by the finance ministry be achieved,” Gemra told the Polish Press Agency (PAP). The government also forecasts, however, that the tax exemption will reduce state budget revenues by nearly 9 billion zloty over 10 years, at a time when public finances are under increasing strain amid rapidly rising debt. Poland’s WIG20 stock market index has hit its highest ever level, surpassing a record that had stood for almost 19 years. The WIG20 has been Europe’s best-performing major blue-chip index so far this year, gaining almost 25% https://t.co/CBbv99v2Uk — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 4, 2026 Poland already has three mechanisms that allow people to accumulate assets with tax advantages: Individual Retirement Accounts (IKE), Individual Pension Schemes (IKZE), and Employee Capital Plans (PPK). However, in all three cases, the capital gains tax exemption is conditional on withdrawing funds after reaching retirement age. Despite the Polish stock market’s strong performance in recent years, Poles’ direct participation remains modest. Shares make up only 2.9% of household assets, the equivalent of 3% of GDP. That is well below the EU average of 8.2%. By contrast, households’ cash holdings are equivalent to 11.5% of GDP, well ahead of the EU average of 4.5% and behind only Slovenia (11.7%) and Germany (11.6%). World.title: Polish PM confirms he wants his “right-hand man” to be made constitutional court judge
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Prime Minister Donald Tusk has confirmed that he will seek to have Maciej Berek, a government minister who stepped down this week and whom Tusk calls his “right-hand man”, appointed as a judge on Poland’s constitutional court. The move has generated considerable controversy given that Tusk’s ruling coalition has repeatedly pledged to “depoliticise” the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) after the previous national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government appointed its former politicians to the court. At a press conference on Thursday, however, Tusk defended the idea, describing Berek as an “apolitical and nonpartisan” figure who would help “fix the Constitutional Tribunal” after it was rendered illegitimate by PiS. Premier @donaldtusk potwierdził, że @MaciejBerek – do tej pory minister ds. nadzoru nad wdrażaniem polityki rządu – będzie kandydatem na sędziego Trybunału Konstytucyjnego. – To jeden z najwybitniejszych polskich prawników – uzasadnił szef rządu.https://t.co/RsKLhLjHhC — PolsatNews.pl (@PolsatNewsPL) August 13, 2026 Berek is a longstanding associate of Tusk. During Tusk’s first period as prime minister, from 2007 to 2014, Berek was head of the Government Legislation Centre (RCL) while also serving as secretary of the cabinet. After Tusk returned to power in 2023, heading a coalition of parties ranging from left to centre right, Berek was appointed as a minister without portfolio and then, in 2025, was made minister in charge of overseeing the implementation of government policy. He has, however, been an extremely low-key figure, rarely speaking in public. Berek is also not a member of parliament, and indeed not even a member of any political party. On Tuesday this week, Tusk unexpectedly announced before a cabinet meeting that Berek, whom he called his “right-hand man”, was leaving the government in order to “move on to other tasks”. The prime minister did not say what those tasks would be, but multiple media outlets reported that Berek would be presented as a candidate to become a judge on the Constitutional Tribunal. Since Tusk’s government came to power in December 2023, it has ignored all TK rulings because three of the tribunal’s judges were appointed illegitimately under the former PiS government. Fifteen months since the change of government, Poland's rule-of-law crisis continues – indeed, many Poles think the situation has got worse.@J_Jaraczewski explains the roots of the crisis, what its impact has been, and how it might be resolved https://t.co/7KOCURV3dU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 The new ruling coalition also criticised the fact that some TK judges were former PiS politicians. Two of them, for example, were appointed in 2019 shortly after stepping down as PiS MPs. Another, the current TK chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, previously served as a deputy justice minister in the PiS government (though he was never a member of the PiS party). When Tusk’s coalition came to power, it promised to restore the legitimacy of the TK, including by “depoliticising” it. In 2024, it approved legislation that would have banned anyone who had served as a politician in the last four years from becoming a TK judge. However, the measures were referred by the then-president, PiS ally Andrzej Duda, to the TK itself, which subsequently declared them unconstitutional, meaning they did not come into force. Poland’s constitutional court has rejected two government bills seeking to overhaul the court itself, with the aim of reversing the politicisation that took place under the former administration. It found that the measures "violate judicial independence" https://t.co/uBJr1bXFv4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 30, 2025 At a press conference on Thursday, Tusk confirmed the rumours that he would seek to make Berek a TK judge. He called Berek “one of the most distinguished Polish legal practitioners, who has made his apolitical and nonpartisan nature a hallmark”. Berek has a doctorate in law and, between his stints in government, worked as an assistant professor in the department of constitutional law at the University of Warsaw. “For him, compliance with the law and the constitution has always been paramount,” declared Tusk. “I don’t know anyone better equipped, better prepared, to help rectify the situation we face with the flawed Constitutional Tribunal.” 💬 Premier @donaldtusk w #Warszawa: Nie mamy żadnych innych interesów w tej sprawie. Zależy nam na naprawieniu Trybunału Konstytucyjnego, żeby nie był na smyczy prezydenta i PiS-u, tylko wykonywał swoją robotę. — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 13, 2026 The prime minister acknowledged that his government had tried to ban politicians from serving on the TK. But he said that Berek himself had recently told him that, “under the current political circumstances, we must do everything we can to remedy the situation” at the tribunal. “Since methods that are unconstitutional are being used from the other side, I must also demonstrate my determination and that we won’t give in to such methods,” added Tusk. Those remarks, in which Tusk also called Święczkowski’s leadership of the TK “embarrassing”, were a reference to the fact that the current PiS-aligned president, Karol Nawrocki, and Święczkowski have refused to accept four new TK judges chosen by parliament earlier this year. “We have no interests in this matter other than to repair the Constitutional Tribunal so that it is not a tool and is not under the thumb of the president or PiS, but rather that it performs its work as objectively as possible,” said Tusk. A newly sworn-in @TK_GOV_PL judge says he will not take his seat until four colleagues appointed by parliament are allowed to take theirs. He said their appointments had been blocked "unlawfully", in the latest twist in a long-running disputehttps://t.co/X30rm1Gfzs — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 29, 2026 However, there remain major potential stumbling blocks on Berek’s path to the TK, not least doubts over whether Tusk’s coalition partners will support his nomination in the Sejm, the lower house of parliament, which is responsible for nominating new TK judges. Anna Maria Żukowska, the head of The Left’s (Lewica) parliamentary caucus, declared on Tuesday that, if rumours of Berek’s nomination were true, “he won’t get votes from The Left because we promised our voters that politicians wouldn’t end up on the TK”. Given that the government has a majority of just nine in the 460-seat Sejm, it would only require a small number of MPs from Tusk’s coalition to oppose Berek’s nomination for him to lose the vote. On Thursday, Tusk said that he “understands” concerns from some coalition partners but that he would “try to convince those who have doubts”. Jeżeli to się wydarzy (a raczej nie), to do niedawna czynny polityk nie dostanie głosów klubu @__Lewica, gdyż obiecaliśmy naszym wyborcom, że politycy nie trafią do TK. Ale IMHO to bardzo krzywdząca dla @MaciejBerek plotka, on by się jako państwowiec w życiu na coś takiego nie… https://t.co/QWFFmdy4V3 — Anna-Maria Żukowska 💁🏻‍♀️ (@AM_Zukowska) August 11, 2026 The next vacancy on the TK’s 15-judge bench is due to open on 18 September, when the nine-year term of Justyn Piskorski, one of the PiS-era judges regarded as illegitimate by the current government, ends. After that, a further vacancy will open in January. However, even if Berek is approved by the Sejm, the law states that new TK judges must swear an oath “before the president”. Nawrocki has used this requirement to refuse to swear in four of the judges chosen by the Sejm this year. He has, however, sworn in three others. It remains unclear what the president would do in the case of Berek. Earlier this week, his chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, told Radio Zet that Nawrocki would “accept the oath if procedures are followed”. However, he added that he does “not know if [the Sejm] is able to carry out those procedures properly”. World.title: Poland reintroduces VAT cut and daily price caps to lower fuel costs for drivers
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s government has announced that, from Monday, it will reintroduce some of the measures that were used earlier this year to lower prices for consumers at petrol stations amid the energy crisis triggered by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The package, known in Polish as CPN and which will be in place from 17 August until at least 31 August, includes reducing VAT on fuels from 23% to 8% and introducing retail consumer price caps on fuels set daily by the energy minister. Announcing the measures on Thursday, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said they should result in prices falling by around 1 zloty (€0.23) per litre. Currently, average retail prices are 7.29 zloty for 95-octane petrol and 8.09 zloty for diesel, according to Polish price monitoring service E-Petrol. 💬 Premier @donaldtusk ⤵️ Polska będzie w absolutnej czołówce europejskiej, jeśli chodzi o najniższe ceny paliw. pic.twitter.com/ar3IZbzFHQ — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 13, 2026 Tusk acknowledged that CPN will entail “serious costs” for the state budget. When similar measures (which also, unlike now, included cuts in excise duty on fuels) were in place between the end of March and end of June, they cost the state an estimated 4.7 billion zloty. On Thursday, the prime minister renewed his criticism of opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki for last month refusing to sign into law a windfall tax on fuel companies’ excess profits this year. The government said that the tax, which would have raised an estimated 4 billion zloty, was intended to help cover the costs of fuel subsidies. The profits of many fuel companies have boomed during the crisis, with Polish state energy giant Orlen last week announcing record half-year results. Nawrocki’s chancellery, however, has argued that fuel companies would seek to pass the costs of tax increases onto consumers, thereby increasing prices. CPN was first introduced in March in response to soaring fuel prices in the wake of US and Israeli attacks on Iran and subsequent disruption to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies. CPN subsequently helped bring Polish fuel prices to among the lowest in the EU. Since the measures were withdrawn in June, prices at the pump in Poland have risen significantly, placing pressure on the government to again cushion the blow for consumers. E-Petrol reports that prices have recently started to fall, but remain well above the levels seen before the crisis. Economists at PKO, a major bank, wrote on Thursday that higher fuel prices in July, which stemmed from the expiry of CPN and an increase in global oil prices, were the main drivers of inflation accelerating from 2.5% in June to 3.0% last month. Polish state energy giant Orlen posted a record profit in the first half of 2026, as turmoil in the Middle East boosted earnings in the fuel sector. Nawrocki’s chief of staff, Zbigniew Bogucki, however, criticised the government for what he claimed was a belated response to high prices. World.title: Polish household assets hit record 4 trillion zloty amid fastest growth in years
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poles are building up wealth at the fastest pace in years, with the combined value of household financial assets surpassing 4 trillion zloty (€930 billion) for the first time, according to new data from the Polish Development Fund (PFR), a state entity. The figure reached 4.1 trillion zloty at the end of the first quarter of this year, up 4.3% from the previous quarter, said PFR. That was the largest quarterly increase in just over six years. On an annual basis, assets rose 15.3%, the fastest pace in five years. After deducting liabilities, household net financial assets stood at 3.2 trillion zloty, also a record. Net assets were up 18.4% from a year earlier and 4.9% from the previous quarter. Ponad 4,1 bln zł – tyle wynoszą już aktywa finansowe polskich gospodarstw domowych. To historyczny rekord. W najnowszej analizie PFR pokazujemy, że w ciągu roku wzrosły o 15,3% – to jedna z najwyższych dynamik w historii. Skala i tempo wzrostu aktywów pokazują też, jak duży jest… pic.twitter.com/fSx1yOZtkn — Mikołaj Raczyński (@MikRaczynski) August 7, 2026 The biggest contribution to the quarterly increase came from what PFR classifies as “other equity holdings”, which include shares in limited liability companies, partnerships, cooperatives and mutual insurance societies. They rose by 61.5 billion zloty. Bank deposits recorded the second-largest increase (44.4 billion zloty). Despite the strong rise in equity holdings, bank deposits and cash remained the largest components of household financial assets, accounting for 26.3% and 11.1% respectively. Pension and disability funds accounted for 10.5% of household financial assets. Meanwhile, shares listed on stock exchanges and regulated over-the-counter markets made up 2.9% of household financial assets. Their value is equivalent to 3% of GDP, one of the lowest shares in the European Union, where the average is 8.2%. Although shares make up only a small share of household assets, the Polish stock market has performed strongly in recent years, with its blue-chip index reaching a record high last week and breaking its previous high set 19 years ago. By contrast, Polish households have a relatively high level of cash holdings. Cash was equivalent to 11.5% of Poland’s GDP in the first quarter, well ahead of the EU average of 4.5% and behind only Slovenia (11.7%) and Germany (11.6%). PFR’s data also show that household liabilities in Poland increased by 5.2% year-on-year to more than 891 billion zloty in the first quarter, well below the rate of asset growth. Long-term loans accounted for 92.2% of liabilities, while short-term loans accounted for 5.1%. Rising household wealth reflects three decades of strong economic growth in Poland, accompanied by a rapid rise in wages and living standards. Earlier this year, state research agency CBOS found that a record 39% of Poles say they are financially comfortable, up from just 3% in the early 1990s. Separate data from Statistics Poland (GUS), a state agency, show that only 2% of the population live in severe deprivation, the lowest level on record. Poland last year rose to its highest-ever level in a measure of household prosperity in European Union member states, overtaking four other countries. That growth has also fuelled a rapid increase in the number of ultra-wealthy people in Poland, whose number has almost doubled since 2019. However, the PFR data show only total combined household assets and liabilities, not how they are distributed across society. World.title: Romanian Community to Celebrate Culture and Traditions in Prague
World.content:
The Romanian community in Czechia will come together in Prague on September 6 for the 12th edition of the Romanian Celebration, an annual event highlighting Romanian culture, traditions and the community’s ties with Czech society.

The main event will take place at the Ethnographic Section of the National Museum of the Czech Republic in Kinský Park, Prague 5.

The program will bring together Romanian music, dance, food, literature and activities for children.



Organized by the Association of Romanians in the Czech Republic (ARRC), the event is part of a wider cultural project running from March 1 to November 30, 2026.

Visitors can expect traditional music and dance performances, educational activities for children, cultural exhibitions, book presentations and Romanian gastronomy.

The event is aimed at members of the Romanian community, Romanian-speaking families, children and young people, as well as Czech residents interested in Romanian culture.

According to ARRC, the project aims to preserve and promote Romanian cultural and linguistic identity among Romanians living in the Czech Republic while creating opportunities for greater interaction between the Romanian and Czech communities.

“Through this project, we aim to offer the Romanian community, Romanian speakers, and lovers of the Romanian language a space for meeting, dialogue, and celebration of our cultural values, while also contributing to the consolidation of intercultural relations between Romania and the Czech Republic,” the ARRC leadership said.

World.title: Czech Fish Farmers Take Emergency Measures Amid Prolonged Drought
World.content:
Fish farmers reduce or suspend supplementary feeding to lower oxygen consumption, reports say.

Fish farmers in the Czech Republic have begun taking emergency measures as a prolonged drought, worsened by high temperatures across Europe, strains water supplies.

Facing water shortages, fish farmers have reduced or suspended supplementary feeding to lower fish oxygen consumption, while ponds are being regularly aerated, according to the report.



Several ponds have also been netted earlier than usual.

In the Třeboň area, which delivers tons of carp for the Czech Christmas table, part of the 200-hectare Koclířov pond has been drained and the fish moved to holding tanks.

More than a third of the water is missing from the region’s famous system of fish ponds due to the drought. The water level in Lake Svět, for example, has fallen by 98 centimetres. High temperatures are also causing water to evaporate more quickly.

The Czech government is expected to address the 2027 budget, upcoming elections and measures to tackle worsening drought.

Prime Minister Andrej Babiš has pledged an extra CZK 4 billion for drought-related measures. If approved, ministers will present plans for implementing them.

World.title: Burgermeister to Open First Prague Restaurant on Wenceslas Square in 2027
World.content:
Berlin burger chain Burgermeister is preparing to enter the Czech market, with its first Prague restaurant expected to open in early 2027.

The company has chosen Wenceslas Square for its debut. The location will also serve as a base for Burgermeister’s planned expansion across the Czech Republic, with more restaurants already in the pipeline.

Burgermeister has built its reputation in Berlin over the past two decades, growing from a single restaurant in a former public toilet into an international chain with 32 locations across Germany and other European markets.



Burgermeister has not yet revealed the exact address or confirmed a specific opening date.

The Prague restaurant will follow the concept that made Burgermeister popular in Berlin. The chain focuses on freshly prepared burgers and fries, with part of its food production handled in-house. Its operations also include its own bakery.

From a former public toilet to an international burger chain

Burgermeister opened its first restaurant in the Kreuzberg district of Berlin in 2006. The location was far from a conventional restaurant site. It occupied a former public toilet beneath the railway tracks near Schlesisches Tor station.

The unusual setting quickly became part of the brand’s identity. Over the years, Burgermeister expanded beyond its original Berlin location and developed into a larger restaurant chain.

Today, the company has 32 branches and is pursuing its goal of building a pan-European network.

World.title: Russell Crowe to Perform in Prague for the First Time in May 2027
World.content:
Oscar-winning actor and musician Russell Crowe will bring his band, The Gentlemen Barbers, to Forum Karlín on May 23, 2027, for their first-ever Prague concert.

Russell Crowe is best known for his roles in Gladiator, A Beautiful Mind and A Good Year, but long before Hollywood, music was a major part of his life.

On May 23, 2027, the Oscar and Golden Globe winner will bring that side of his career to Prague for the first time, performing with his band The Gentlemen Barbers at Forum Karlín.



You can get your ticket here.

The concert will also mark the opening night of the band’s European tour.

The Gentlemen Barbers have been developing their sound over the past four years, although many of the musicians have worked with Crowe for decades. The lineup includes drummer Dave Kelly and trumpeter Stewart Kirwan, both former members of Thirty Odd Foot of Grunts, as well as musicians who have collaborated with Crowe on later projects.

The band also features pianist Stu Hunter, guitarist Chris Kamzelas and bassist James Hazelwood. Irish singer Lorraine O’Reilly, known for her powerful, raspy vocals, has performed with Crowe since they first met while recording a duet for the Bible Code Sundays album Walk Like Kings.

The result is a band that moves between R&B, gospel, country, dark waltzes and singalong anthems, with storytelling at the centre of its music.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by JV Classics (@jvclassics)

“There is an attitude about this band. It’s got a groove. We do a lot of story songs, but we also know we are here to blow out cobwebs and give the audience a good night,” Crowe says.

For Crowe, music has remained a constant alongside his film career. He began performing in bands, touring and releasing records before moving into musical theatre and eventually film. He has continued to perform throughout his decades in Hollywood, despite his demanding acting career.

“I love playing in pubs. It’s what I did growing up. Even though my day job has a huge claim on my time, I’ve never not played music,” he says.

Russell Crowe’s Indoor Garden Party & The Gentlemen Barbers takes place on May 23, 2027, at 8 p.m. at Forum Karlín in Prague.

World.title: How Much Can a Prague Taxi Driver Really Earn Each Month
World.content:
For passengers, a taxi ride can make the job look straightforward. Pick someone up, drive them across Prague, wait for the next booking and repeat.

But the income of a full-time taxi driver depends on far more than the fare shown on the meter or app.

Drivers working through platforms such as Uber and Bolt can generate more than CZK 60,000 in gross monthly revenue when working around 40 to 50 hours a week. What they actually keep, however, is considerably less.



Gross income can exceed CZK 60,000

Official figures for Prague’s taxi sector put the average gross monthly pay at roughly CZK 38,000. Drivers who work full time through ride-hailing platforms can earn more, particularly when they concentrate on periods of high demand.

According to Ondřej Krátký, founder of the Czech taxi platform Liftago, drivers can typically earn about CZK 250 to CZK 350 per hour. At the lower end of the market, however, some drivers make only around CZK 80 an hour, which is difficult to turn into a sustainable income in Prague.

Official statistics may also underestimate the money generated by some drivers because not every journey is paid through an app. Cash payments remain part of the business.

Fuel and commissions take a large share

Most Prague taxi drivers operate as self-employed contractors and use their own cars. That means they are responsible for almost all of the costs associated with the job.

Fuel is one of the largest expenses. Someone driving every day can spend more than CZK 10,000 a month on petrol or diesel alone.

Ride-hailing platforms also take a percentage of each fare. Depending on the service and other conditions, commissions can account for roughly 20 to 25 percent of the fare. Drivers must also cover vehicle maintenance, repairs, commercial insurance and the mandatory social and health insurance payments required of self-employed workers.

Once these expenses are taken into account, the amount left from gross earnings can fall by a third or more.

For a full-time driver, a realistic monthly amount after operating costs can therefore be somewhere between CZK 22,000 and CZK 35,000. The exact figure depends on the car, fuel consumption, working hours, platform commissions and the number and type of trips completed.

Tips make only a small difference

Tips are unlikely to transform a taxi driver’s income in the Czech Republic.

Unlike in countries where tipping is a major part of service workers’ earnings, Czech passengers generally round up the fare or leave a relatively small amount.

Uber allows passengers to tip through its app for up to 30 days after a journey, with the full tip going to the driver. Bolt offers a similar feature.

For most drivers, however, tips remain a minor addition to their monthly income rather than a significant source of earnings.

Timing can make a bigger difference

Drivers can increase their income by choosing when and where they work.

Friday and Saturday nights are among the busiest periods in Prague, particularly in the city centre. When demand rises sharply, ride-hailing platforms can increase fares, allowing drivers to generate more revenue from the same number of working hours.

Major concerts, festivals and other large events can have a similar effect. Airport journeys can also be attractive because they tend to cover longer distances than short trips within the city.

World.title: Czechia Now Ranks Among the World’s 10 Best Countries to Live In
World.content:
Czechia has placed ninth among 192 countries in the 2026 Rumavi Global Relocation Index, which assesses destinations based on factors including safety, healthcare, taxation, living costs and opportunities for people considering a move abroad.

The country scored 69.9 points in the overall ranking, putting it just outside the top five but ahead of Malta and several larger European economies. Estonia took first place with 72.8 points, followed by Singapore, Malaysia, Portugal and Taiwan.

Czechia performed particularly well in the ranking for families, where it placed third worldwide. The index also gave the country strong scores for safety, property rights and climate risk.



Within Europe, Czechia ranked fourth overall. Estonia, Portugal and Lithuania were the only European countries placed higher in the general ranking.

The results are based on the Rumavi Global Relocation Index 2026, a privately produced ranking designed for people considering relocation as well as investors. Rumavi evaluates 192 countries using 24 indicators grouped into four areas: finance and taxes, livability and health, safety and stability, and settling and opportunity.

Czechia scores particularly well for families

The index uses different weightings for different types of people considering a move. For families, safety, education, cost of living and healthcare carry greater weight than tax considerations.

Czechia’s overall result is less impressive for other groups. It ranked 20th among countries assessed for retirees and 25th for digital nomads.

The index also evaluates destinations for entrepreneurs and people primarily interested in tax efficiency, although the rankings can vary significantly depending on the category.

What the index measures

Rumavi says its ranking is intended to measure the practical conditions faced by someone moving to another country rather than simply assessing tourism or passport access.

The 24 indicators cover issues such as affordability, income tax, foreign-income taxation, banking, healthcare, housing, air quality, climate, digital infrastructure, education, business opportunities, language, visa access, property rights and startup ecosystems.

Each indicator is converted to a score between zero and 100, with higher scores representing more favorable conditions for someone relocating. The same data is then weighted differently for six groups: general applicants, retirees, digital nomads, families, entrepreneurs and people seeking tax advantages.

For the general ranking, the most heavily weighted indicators include street safety, foreign-income taxation, cost of living and climate comfort.

Rumavi’s methodology draws on sources including the World Bank, World Health Organization, OECD, World Justice Project, UNODC and other international datasets. Some indicators, including visa access, property rights for non-citizens and aspects of taxation, are classified as Rumavi assessments rather than direct institutional data.

World.title: Passenger Attacks Four Airport Staff After Being Denied Boarding in Prague
World.content:
A passenger attacked four employees of ground-handling company Menzies Aviation at Prague’s Airport on Thursday evening after being denied boarding on a flight to Rome.

The incident took place at Terminal 2, near Gate C9, shortly after 8 p.m., according to Zdopravy.cz.

The woman arrived late for boarding on a Ryanair flight. After being refused entry to the aircraft, she reportedly became aggressive and attacked members of the ground-handling staff.



One of the employees stepped between the woman and a colleague who was being confronted by her. The passenger then bit him.

Airport police were called to the scene and used restraint equipment to detain the woman. She was subsequently escorted from the boarding area and handed over to the Czech police.

“The woman was late for the boarding gate, and after being denied boarding, she physically attacked an airport employee,” Josef Urban, a spokesperson for the Foreign Police Directorate said.

“Responding officers detained her using restraint equipment, and the case is now being investigated as disorderly conduct,” he added.

The incident was also confirmed by Prague Airport spokesperson Jiří Hánich.

The injured employees required medical treatment following the attack. Four members of the Menzies team were reportedly involved in the incident.

Menzies Aviation has operated at Václav Havel Airport Prague since 1991. The company provides ground-handling services covering passengers, baggage, aircraft and cargo for a significant share of flights at the airport.

World.title: Around 300 Czech Citizens Evacuated Due to Fire in Croatia
World.content:
Some 300 Czech tourists are among the 1,000 evacuees with a Czech police officer sent to coordinate the emergency response.

Croatian prime minister Andrej Plenković is in the town holding a coordination meeting with all emergency services this morning. Croatian president Zoran Milanović is also expected later today.

“All those injured in last night’s fire are being provided with the necessary medical care,” Plenković said in an earlier update on X.

No fatalities have been reported. The spokesman said there were also no reports of serious injuries among Czech citizens.

Some tourists left the area on their own, while others are staying at evacuation centres in Omiš and Split. A Czech consul is on site and is in contact with local authorities and security forces.

Fire spreads across up to 1,000 hectares

Around 160 firefighters, supported by specialised firefighting aircraft, are battling the blaze.

The fire has caused significant material damage, according to eyewitnesses, with dozens of cars and homes reportedly destroyed. Strong winds have helped the flames spread across an area estimated at between 900 and 1,000 hectares.

Witnesses reported hearing gas cylinders exploding inside burning homes, while the streets were filled with the sirens of fire engines, ambulances and police vehicles. Large parts of Omiš have also been left without electricity.

Mass evacuation underway

Hundreds of people have fled the affected area, with some tourists escaping by boat, catamaran and other small vessels.

The organised evacuation is being coordinated through the Ribnjak sports hall in Omiš. From there, evacuees are being transported by bus to the Gripe sports centre in Split.

According to Omiš fire chief Slavko Tucaković, foreigners make up the majority of those evacuated.

World.title: Hungary’s finest cave bath reopens on national holiday – what to expect on prices, programs
World.content:
Miskolctapolca’s Cave Bath, one of Hungary’s most striking thermal attractions, is set to reopen its doors on August 20, marking the end of a nearly two-year closure following a devastating fire. The city is pulling out all the stops for the occasion, with a packed programme of events planned across Miskolc for the long holiday weekend.

A troubled return

The bath suffered severe fire damage on September 6, 2024, when flames broke out in the aqua therapy section before spreading to other parts of the complex. While the outdoor pools escaped relatively lightly and were brought back into use the following summer, the cave section itself required extensive reconstruction, with work beginning in late 2025. From August 20, visitors will once again be able to bathe in the thermal pools hewn into the natural cave passages, though the medical and therapeutic facilities will remain closed for the time being.

Heartbreaking images after the 2024 fire:

Admission prices at the restored cave bath

An all-day adult ticket to the cave bath will cost 8,500 forints, with reduced rates of 6,400 forints for children, students and pensioners. Miskolc residents benefit from further discounts: 5,100 forints for adults and 3,800 forints for children, students and pensioners.

Three-hour tickets are also available: 6,000 forints for adults and 4,500 forints for concessionary categories, or 2,400 and 1,800 forints respectively for locals.

The outdoor Shell Beach. Photo: Miskolctapolca Cave Bath and Aquatherapy

Family tickets for a full day are priced at 18,700 forints for two adults and one child, and 11,900 forints for one adult and one child; each additional child costs 5,100 forints. The three-hour family rates are 14,000 and 8,900 forints, with extra children at 3,800 forints.

Group tickets (from 15 people) are offered at 7,300 forints for adults and 5,500 forints for children, students and pensioners. Disabled visitors pay a reduced rate of 3,800 forints, according to Pénzcentrum.

If you missed: Hungarian Wizz Air opens new base in another European city!

A city-wide celebration

The reopening will be accompanied by a four-day festival, “Pezsgés Miskolctapolcán” (Fizzing in Miskolctapolca), running from August 20 to 23, with concerts, food events and community activities.

Elsewhere in the city, the airport will host “Legends in the Air” from August 20 to 22, featuring air displays, rare aircraft and family entertainment, including a presentation by aerobatic pilot Péter Bessenyei.

In the city centre, the “Tündöklő” (Radiant) Light Festival on August 20 and 21 will project installations and films onto public buildings and spaces.On August 20, Miskolc Zoo will mark its 43rd anniversary with a day of birthday events, while on the evening of August 22 the Night Run Miskolc will set off from Szent István Square, with 5km, 10km and 21km routes.

World.title: Personal documentary is being made about former PM Viktor Orbán – here’s its main focus
World.content:
A “personal documentary” directed by Réka Pigniczky is being made in Hungarian-Canadian co-production about former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán’s political “transformation and downfall”, with the premiere scheduled for the first half of 2027, the Hungarian film portal Filmhu has reported.

The documentary project titled Orbán and Me was presented on Sunday at the Cinelink Industry Days professional forum at the Sarajevo Film Festival, the website said. Pigniczky’s project was selected, alongside six other films in production, for the professional forum dubbed “Docu Talents From the East”, organised by the Jihlava International Documentary Film Festival in Czechia. On Monday, the jury will award a prize to the most promising project, MTI wrote.

According to the Jihlava Festival’s website, Orbán and Me is “an intimate political documentary” in which Pigniczky — who had previously interviewed Orban — attempted to speak again with the then Prime Minister during the 2026 Hungarian parliamentary elections.

The filmmaker “seeks to understand his transformation from democratic reformer to increasingly inaccessible leader”. Through the attempt to interview Orbán, and the debates within the director’s own family, “the film explores democracy’s fragility, political polarisation, and whether democratic renewal remains possible in Hungary today,” the Jihlava Festival website said.

World.title: How to see a doctor without insurance in Budapest: a tourist’s guide
World.content:
You wake up in your Budapest hotel feeling much worse than you did yesterday. Perhaps you’ve developed a high fever overnight, food poisoning has ruined your sightseeing plans, or you’ve injured yourself exploring the city. As you reach for your phone to find a doctor, you realize something that makes the situation even more stressful. You forgot to buy travel insurance.

Written by: Dorottya Fekete

Collaborative content

If you need to see a doctor without insurance in Budapest, you can still receive medical care at a private clinic, although you will normally pay directly for your treatment.

Remember, your health is important, and resources are available to help you get care even if you’re uninsured. Knowing your options in advance can make it easier to navigate the healthcare system and decide where to seek appropriate care.

Where Can Tourists See a Doctor Without Insurance in Budapest?

Rest assured, there are several ways to see a doctor without insurance in Budapest. Healthcare services are accessible to tourists in Budapest, whether for vacation or business. Waiting times and English-language support can vary between public healthcare facilities, so it’s useful to check what services are available to international visitors before attending.

Private clinics such as FirstMed offer outpatient medical care for international visitors, including English-language communication with doctors and reception staff. Appointments are available during regular opening hours, subject to availability. You’ll understand the recommended care and its rationale, and you’ll receive medical documents in English, which can be useful for follow-up after returning home.

EHIC and GHIC: Do They Replace Private Insurance?

Many travelers wonder whether the European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) or, for UK travelers, the Global Health Insurance Card (GHIC) offers similar access to medical care as travel insurance. But this is not the case. The EHIC/GHIC covers only medically necessary care at public/statutory facilities during a temporary stay and isn’t valid at private clinics. You can also access private medical care smoothly, but you’ll need to pay for the services out of pocket.

Difference between travel insurance and EHIC/GHIC:

EHIC/GHIC:

Provides access to the public healthcare system for medically necessary issues;

Excludes cancellation or travel back to your home country;

Doesn’t cover the costs of private treatment.

Travel Insurance: depending on the terms and conditions of the specific policy, it may

Cover eligible private medical treatment.

Reimburse eligible private healthcare costs;

Include cancellations and return travel/transportation.

Private Healthcare Cost for Tourists in Budapest

Concerns regarding unpredictable out-of-pocket expenses often make travelers hesitant to see a doctor without insurance in Budapest.

Many common health concerns can initially be assessed during a doctor’s consultation. Depending on the diagnosis, the doctor may recommend treatment, prescribe medication, or arrange further testing or follow-up.

To ensure you stay on budget, it is advisable to inquire about payment terms in advance. Ask about consultation fees, additional tests or procedures, and any documentation charges before treatment if you need to understand the expected cost.

Even if you are currently uninsured, keep your invoices and medical records in case you later need them for your records or for an insurance claim. However, any reimbursement will depend on the terms of your insurance policy.

What does a private doctor visit typically include for a tourist?

FirstMed provides outpatient medical care in English for international visitors, including consultations with English-speaking doctors. The clinic provides English-language communication with doctors and reception staff, helping international visitors understand their care. Open every day excluding holidays, the clinic may be able to offer same-day appointments for urgent, non-life-threatening health concerns, depending on availability.

Tourist looking to see a doctor without insurance in Budapest, in front of Hattyúház, building of FirstMed, English-speaking clinic.Source: FirstMed

Depending on your symptoms and the doctor’s assessment, your FirstMed appointment may include:

A consultation with an English-speaking doctor

Discussion of your symptoms and medical history

A physical examination

Recommendation for treatment and further care

Prescriptions for medications available in Hungary

Referral for hospital care if your condition requires emergency or complex treatment.

Additional diagnostic testing or specialist consultations may be recommended and obtained in-house depending on your symptoms and the doctor’s assessment.

What should you bring to your appointment?

Bring your passport or other photo ID, a payment card or cash in local currency (such as HUF), a list of regular medications, details about allergies or chronic health conditions, your EHIC or GHIC if available (for administrative purposes, as it is not accepted for payment), and any available medical documents related to your current illness or injury.

If English isn’t your first language, it can also help to keep a note of your symptoms on your phone, including when they started, any medications you’ve taken, and whether they’ve been improving or worsening.

If you’re feeling unwell, it’s easy to forget important details. Gathering these key items in advance can help your appointment run more smoothly.

Conclusion

Without insurance, medical care in Hungary is available but must be paid for. EHIC/GHIC can provide access to medically necessary healthcare within the public healthcare system, but it does not cover private medical care. For international visitors considering private treatment, English-language communication and appointment availability may be important factors.

At an international private clinic in Budapest like FirstMed, tourists can arrange care without insurance and be seen in English. That lets you focus on recovery rather than paperwork.

Before booking, check the clinic’s current consultation fees for English-language services and ask whether additional tests or procedures may involve extra charges.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) About Seeing a Doctor Without Insurance

How can I find a doctor in Budapest without insurance? You can find a doctor without insurance at both public and private clinics in Budapest. Private international clinics, such as FirstMed, may be an option for visitors who specifically want English-language communication and appointment-based care. Public hospitals might have long wait times for non-emergency cases, and there’s no assurance you’ll find an English-speaking doctor. Do private clinics accept EHIC in Hungary? Unfortunately, EHIC or GHIC cannot be used to pay for treatment at private clinics. EHIC/GHIC cards are intended for access to medically necessary healthcare within the applicable public/statutory healthcare system and are not a form of private health insurance.

If you choose a private clinic for appointment-based care and English-language communication, you will need to pay directly for the medical services you receive. How much does it cost to see a doctor without insurance in Budapest? In Budapest, the costs of seeing a doctor without insurance depend on whether you choose a private clinic or the public system. EHIC/GHIC holders can access medically necessary treatment in the public healthcare network, though some fees or services may apply. Tourists who are not eligible for EHIC/GHIC coverage, or who prefer to use private healthcare, can contact a private clinic to ask about consultation fees and available appointment options. Is an urgent care doctor available without insurance? Private clinics may offer appointments for urgent, non-emergency health concerns, depending on availability. Calling the clinic at least one hour before your arrival allows the staff to prepare for your specific symptoms, secure your slot, and minimize your wait, helping you get back to your travels sooner. Shall I book an appointment, or can I walk in? Some private clinics can see you the same day, but it is highly recommended to schedule an appointment rather than walk in. Calling a clinic even one hour before you arrive allows the staff to prepare for your specific symptoms, reserve a time slot, and minimize your wait. You can also double-check the expected treatment costs.

World.title: Could the August 20 fireworks be cancelled? Looming peril threatens Budapest
World.content:
As the August 20 fireworks approach, forecast uncertainty invariably rises, for late summer brings a confluence of atmospheric influences to the Carpathian Basin. This volatility, coupled with the sudden onset of violent showers and thunderstorms, could place the national day celebrations in jeopardy. There is precedent: a few years ago the display was called off over fears of an approaching storm, while in 2006 an inhuman gale that broke during the fireworks themselves left five dead and hundreds injured.

Forecasting August 20 remains notoriously difficult

The Carpathian Basin’s hitherto monotonous summer weather is now shifting. This morning, a continuous cloud layer obscured the sun over Budapest, and a brief shower drenched the capital and its environs in the small hours. For weeks there had been no rain to speak of, nor even cloudy skies; a scorching heatwave had baked Hungary and the surrounding region.

Storms after heatwave. Photo: Anadolu/Németi Róbert

A significant atmospheric reorganisation is under way, yet the heat is not retreating – and that combination may render the national holiday genuinely hazardous. Cool, 12–22°C dawns will be followed by daytime highs of 30–35°C, conditions that readily spawn violent showers and thunderstorms. The meteorological service has therefore issued lemon-yellow warnings for several counties, as reported by Blikk. Precisely what to expect on Thursday remains exceptionally difficult to predict.

On multiple occasions, forecasters have only been able to confirm at the last moment that no major storm would materialise; conversely, events have been cancelled on the basis of such warnings.

Ominous precedents

In 2022, for example, forecasts indicated a serious storm threatening the capital. When the prediction ultimately proved erroneous, the Government dismissed the then president and deputy president of the National Meteorological Service. The fireworks were held a week later, on August 27.On August 20, 2006, however, the display was not called off in time. A storm arriving with winds of 120 km/h struck the celebrating capital. Five people died and more than 300 were injured; the Orbán government in 2022 was determined to avoid any repeat of that catastrophe.

Photo: Facebook/Magyarország Kormánya

If you missed: ‘People were shouting, trapped beneath the seats’ – exclusive interview, video and latest developments in Polish bus crash

A radical shift in Hungary’s weather

At present, meteorologists are expecting partly cloudy, sunny conditions on August 20, but showers and thunderstorms could break out almost anywhere owing to the persistent heat and elevated mean temperatures.

According to an analysis by The Weather on Maps, the heatwave-inducing air mass is drifting eastwards and weakening, while a cool oceanic–Arctic air mass is advancing; their frontal boundary will undulate over our region, definitively ending the recent weather monotony. This, however, introduces another uncertainty factor for the fireworks. It is also the change that may bring more substantial rainfall to the upper catchment of the Danube and thus assist Paks.

Ongoing heroic work near the Paks NPP to raise the water level of the drying Danube and provide enough cooling water for the plant. Photo: Facebook/Péter Magyar

On the national holiday, therefore, everyone would do well to keep abreast of the expected weather – and then no one should be caught unawares.

World.title: PM Magyar’s stern message to richest Hungarian Lőrinc Mészáros over scheme to aid very poor, but high-achieving students
World.content:
Prime Minister Péter Magyar called on MBH Bank and Lőrinc Mészáros, who has ties to business interests with stakes in the lender, to reinstate a charity programme benefitting children from low-income households with good grades in a post on Facebook on Monday.

New HQ of Lőrinc Mészáros’s bank too expensive?

Magyar said that the International Children’s Safety Service had announced that MBH Bank had pulled support for the programme, after 32 years, while moving forward with the construction of a new corporate headquarters, “in an untransparent manner”, at a cost of more than HUF 100bn.

Lőrinc Mészáros and former FM Péter Szijjártó. The latter is now a top executive of the Chinese BYD. Photo: FB/Szijjártó

In the name of the state of Hungary, which is also a stakeholder in MBH Bank, Magyar called on Mészáros and MBH Bank to publish the details of the new HQ, including the plans and the name of the general contractor, MTI wrote.

MBH Bank, Hungary’s second-largest commercial lender, is listed on the Budapest Stock Exchange. A little more than 25pc of the bank’s shares are in free float.

Péter Magyar wrote in a Facebook post that Mészáros’s bank had helped 100 low‑income, high‑achieving students under a programme it now plans to cancel.

Hungary’s richest reshaped by the Orbán era: Mészáros wealth surges by 284,400% in 15 years!

The bank responded

The scholarship was open to outstanding students from families whose per‑capita monthly income was below HUF 55,000 (about €151). Recipients received HUF 800,000 a year (roughly €2,200), equivalent to around €183 per month.The bank’s full‑year profit for 2025 stood at HUF 240 billion (€661 million).

In response to a statement by the International Children’s Safety Service, the bank said it was “baffled” that the organisation had taken the matter to the press. MBH Bank stated that its decision to withdraw from the programme had been made last year and that the organisation had been given a year to prepare for the consequences. The bank did not respond directly to Péter Magyar’s remarks, but added that it had spent “tens of millions of forints” on the scheme in recent years.

World.title: Details emerge for this year’s August 20 celebrations: beer prices, performers, concerts – and PM Magyar moonlighting as a DJ?
World.content:
Just as on May 9 at his inauguration, PM Péter Magyar is expected to take his place once more behind the DJ decks on Kossuth Square, in front of the Hungarian Parliament. Yet the August 20 celebrations for Hungary’s National Day will not be confined to this central stage: parties are also planned in front of the Technical University and on Margaret Island. And, reassuringly for revellers, beer will not be prohibitively expensive. The details follow.

End of generous subsidies on August 20

According to the latest information from Telex, discounted beer prices will once again feature at this year’s August 20 celebrations in Budapest – though they will be considerably higher than last year’s. In previous years, the Orbán governments took great care to ensure that certain products remained exceptionally cheap during the national day festivities. Thus, draught Borsodi (0.4l) could be had for as little as 380 forints, while a canned version (0.5l) cost 430 forints. Wine was also inexpensive (260 forints per decilitre), as were pálinka, mineral water, Viennese pretzels and Coca-Cola or Pepsi.

August 20 celebrations in Budapest before. Photo: FB

This year, however, the new government is no longer subsidising these prices so generously, meaning costs will rise significantly – albeit still below full market rates. The reason is that, while there is no direct subsidy, a price cap remains in place: no vendor will be permitted to sell beer for more than 1,000 forints or mineral water for more than 500 forints.

These terms were set by the event organiser, Centrum Production. Partly due to the absence of state price support, the celebration itself will be considerably cheaper to stage: the Tisza government intends to run the entire affair on a budget of just 4 billion forints.

The military show is a traditional part of the August 20 celebrations. Source: FB/Hungarian Government

A shorter fireworks display – and DJ Péter Magyar?

In return, even the traditionally spectacular fireworks will be briefer. The fireworks, held every year since the 1930s, will not be cancelled this year, but will last only 10 minutes. By way of contrast, last year’s display ran for 30 minutes, commissioned by the then government with a pronounced focus on King Peter Orseolo, one of Saint Stephen’s successors (1038–1041; 1044–1046), implicitly drawing an unflattering parallel between that controversial figure and the then opposition leader, now Prime Minister, Péter Magyar.

Alongside the fireworks and the pricier beer, there will be numerous free, open-air events on August 19 and 20 across three venues. On both days, the Danube embankment in front of the Technical University will host Elektro Rakpart, featuring a host of performers, while Kossuth Square will transform into Diszkótér, with acts including Anima Sound System.

The traditional fireworks over Budapest: this year it will be cheaper and shorter. Photo: Facebook/Magyarország Kormánya

Whether Péter Magyar will again step behind the DJ console – as he did on May 9 at his inauguration – remains a mystery. What is certain, according to Telex, is that a number of surprise guests have yet to be announced.

Traffic changed due to the 20 August celebrations – check out the details in our article

On Margaret Island, alternative music and guitars will take centre stage on both days. Among the acts scheduled to appear are Quimby, and there will also be an LGT tribute concert courtesy of Random Trip. For full details, readers are directed to the Telex article.

August 20 celebrations: what for?

August 20 is Hungary’s red-letter day, the nation’s official state holiday, commemorating the foundation of the state and Saint Stephen, the first Christian king of Hungary. King Stephen, canonised in 1083 (reigned 997/1000–1038), continued the state- and church-building “work” of his father, Grand Prince Géza (972–997), integrating Hungary into the Christian European world. To this end, he overcame rival claimants to the throne and domestic opponents, while also successfully repelling external interference. By the end of his reign, Hungary was a young state with a solid administrative structure, firmly part of Christian Europe – one that successfully weathered the turbulent decades following Stephen’s death (1038–1046).

The portrait of St Stephen made by an unnamed artist who could see the king with his own eyes more than a millenium ago – read our article to find out where you can check it out. Photo: Creative Commons

Major changes are coming to Hungary’s 20 August celebrations this year: here’s what’s in store

World.title: Invasive mosquito species conquering Hungary – climate change destroys our echosystem?
World.content:
Drought has driven native mosquitoes from much of Hungary, only for invasive species—chiefly the Asian tiger mosquito—to thrive in residential areas, the National Directorate General for Disaster Management (OKF) has warned.

Mosquito patterns shaped by drought

Across most of the country, dry weather continues to dictate the appearance of biting mosquitoes: the floodplain species that often cause significant nuisance along rivers are barely to be seen this season, whereas invasive species are increasingly present in residential areas, particularly Asian tiger mosquitoes, the OKF said. In a statement on Monday, the directorate noted that tiger mosquito larvae can develop in large numbers in as little as a glassful of water, so after rain or garden watering numerous ideal breeding sites spring up around homes, MTI wrote.

An Aedes albopictus (Asian tiger mosquito) female mosquito obtaining a blood meal from a human host. Source: Wikimedia Commons/James Gathany/CDC

Where native larvae still survive

For the larvae of Hungary’s native mosquitoes, suitable habitat has all but disappeared, with the exception of the Tisza Lake area, where fluctuating water levels create favourable conditions for development. There, on stretches not covered by nature conservation protection, specialists are carrying out both biological larviciding and treatments targeting adult mosquitoes.

Limits of organised control over invasives

The breeding sites of invasive mosquitoes lie beyond the reach of organised intervention, since the overwhelming majority form on private property. Where their numbers become overwhelming, treatments are conducted after sunset, in the late evening and night hours, using spraying equipment mounted on flatbed vehicles, officials said.

Where spraying vehicles will appear

In the coming days, mosquito-control vehicles can be expected in several settlements in Baranya, Borsod-Abaúj-Zemplén and Békés counties, with targeted partial treatments planned in one district of Budapest and in certain neighbourhoods of Szeged. A detailed list of affected settlements with planned control dates is available on the disaster management website, while residents can also follow updates on the official media channels of the relevant local councils.
